EOP-34.renderedBody:
Delivered on branch EOP-34-h2-artifact-hardening, PR #110 (three commits: 0e28e0b, 0a744d7, 57c1974), cut from main at f1baad6. Recorded as [ADR-047|docs/adr/ADR-047-h2-excluded-from-deployable-artifact.md].

Disposition against the acceptance criteria

Scenario 1 — satisfied, but by a different mechanism than item 1 proposed. org/h2/server/web/JakartaWebServlet.class is absent from the repackaged jar, and ./mvnw verify is green including the EOP-27 tripwire. The mechanism is <excludes> on the spring-boot-maven-plugin repackage execution, not <scope>test</scope>. The criterion was written about the artifact, and the artifact is what changed.

Scenario 2 — satisfied. ./mvnw spring-boot:run on the default profile still starts against in-memory H2: /health returned 200 after 5s with Database dialect: H2Dialect and Started Main in 3.696 seconds, no errors. So the second limb of Scenario 2 — closing the scope half as won't-do — was not needed, because local development was never disturbed.

Scenario 3 — not applicable. Item 2 is declined; see below.

Item 1 — delivered in substance, not in letter

The scope stays runtime. Moving it to test would break every local ./mvnw spring-boot:run, a path pinned by README.md, SETUP.md, docs/devops/local-development.md, ADR-008, ADR-021, ADR-035 and — decisively — by ADR-012, which states the default profile path "is a decision, not a defect, and should not be 'fixed' later". Moving the default profile to PostgreSQL instead was also rejected: it destroys clone-and-run, needs an ADR-012 amendment plus four document changes, and buys hardening of a path that does not compile today (see the correction below).

Excluding H2 from the artifact instead gets the durable property the ticket wanted — the 13 org.h2.server.web classes are gone from the jar that runs on EC2, and every deployed configuration runs the prod profile against PostgreSQL, so the artifact never needed H2 — while leaving local development and all H2-dependent tests untouched. It is also independent of scope: if someone later widens the dependency to compile, the classes still cannot reach the artifact.

A correction to the ticket's premise

The ticket states a console is reachable today "with zero dependency changes" via new ServletRegistrationBean<>(new JakartaWebServlet(), "/h2-console") or org.h2.tools.Server.createWebServer(...).start(). Neither compiles. runtime scope already keeps H2 off the compile classpath — settled by writing a probe class referencing org.h2.tools.Server and compiling it, which failed with package org.h2.tools does not exist. The residual reachable path is reflection, or a second reviewed change widening the scope first. The gap was real and worth closing; it was narrower than stated, and both the ADR and the changelog say so.

Note for anyone verifying this: dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.includeScope=compile is misleading here — it lists h2-2.4.240.jar anyway. A real compile is the only reliable check.

Item 2 — declined, with reason

No maven-enforcer ban on org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-h2console, on @security-auditor's own EOP-27 reasoning: "a ban with no sanctioned escape hatch trains people to disable bans." H2ConsoleAbsentIntegrationTest is the better control because it is satisfiable — it fires at review time and a reviewer is its escape hatch. The two controls are complementary rather than redundant: the tripwire guards the autoconfiguration path, the new gate guards the artifact. Declining also keeps the declared Maven plugin count at six. @security-auditor re-reviewed this decision on the PR and ruled it defensible.

The gate, and its honest limits

tools/artifact/assert-no-h2-in-jar.sh runs in CI's build job — the only required check on main — between ./mvnw verify and Upload artifact, so nothing unverified is published. Four checks: exactly one jar; PostgreSQL driver present as a positive control; no BOOT-INF/lib/h2-.jar; no org/h2/* entries anywhere, which catches H2 arriving flattened or under other coordinates.

Proven to fail in both directions, not just to pass: restoring main's pom.xml and repackaging makes it exit 1 with FAIL: H2 is back inside the artifact, and pointing it at an empty directory also exits 1 rather than passing vacuously.

Two accepted residuals are recorded rather than glossed:

  1. On a laptop, ./mvnw spring-boot:run still has H2 on the runtime classpath, so a reflectively-registered console remains possible locally against a scratch in-memory database. This gates the artifact, not the workstation.
  2. ./mvnw spring-boot:run and java -jar now have different classpaths. ADR-012's thesis is byte-identical configuration, which is untouched; @architecture-guardian ruled ADR-047's recording sufficient and ADR-012 not in need of amendment. The divergence is bounded to one dependency the prod profile never loads, and fails loudly rather than silently. ADR-047 carries a revisit trigger if the default profile ever gains a deployed role.

Definition of Done — all five gates approved

Gate Verdict
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE (re-review after remediation: 0 blockers, 0 majors, 0 mediums, 0 lows)
@architecture-guardian APPROVE
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE

./mvnw clean verify green throughout: 1256 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, SpotBugs 0, coverage met (96% instruction, 88% branch over 141 classes). @tester-unit-and-quality independently confirmed the suite is unaffected — runtime scope still puts H2 on the test classpath, so all the jdbc:h2:mem: migration tests and their pinned H2 SQL states are untouched — and that the EOP-27 tripwire still runs, with none of its four assertions made newly vacuous.

Two defects found during the gate round and fixed rather than accepted

@code-reviewer found the claim "no test could gate this" overstated: maven-failsafe-plugin is already available at 3.5.6 from the Boot parent and binds after package, so a failsafe IT genuinely could do it. Only surefire is blocked. Narrowed at all four sites — one of which nobody had spotted in the first round — and the failsafe alternative is now recorded with its single rejection ground (it would be a seventh declared plugin) and a revisit trigger.

Separately, an exact jar-size delta was withdrawn rather than corrected. pom.xml is embedded in the artifact under BOOT-INF/classes/META-INF/maven/, so editing a comment in it grows the jar — which falsified a figure a reviewer had already verified arithmetically. The delta was fragile by construction, since it compares jars built from different poms. Replaced with durable facts, and each site says why no exact delta is given so a future author does not restore one.

Implementation complete and awaiting human review.

PR: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/89

Branch: eop-35-liquibase-contexts-adr — 5 commits off origin/main (e33ec89)

All four acceptance criteria met

AC Verification
1 — rule entry reduced, names no library version `awk 'NR==37' .opencode/rules/database.md |grep -oE 'Liquibase [0-9]+'` → no match. 1859 → 1341 bytes
2 — new ADR with house structure, matrix, javap mechanisms, versions docs/adr/ADR-043-liquibase-contexts-are-not-used.md — Status/Date/Deciders, 21-encoding matrix, three discard mechanisms, resolved-versions table
3 — index row satisfies AdrIndexConsistencyTest All five invariants pass; verified by three separate gates
4 — no version-pinned claim left in .opencode/rules/ Swept independently by three gates; InfluxDB 1.8 and Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 ruled out of scope (tool/spec versions with dated ADR homes)

Definition of Done — all five gates approve the merge tree

Gate Verdict Tree
@architecture-guardian APPROVE (4th round) fc8ec3f
@code-reviewer APPROVE (re-dispatched) fc8ec3f
@security-auditor APPROVE (re-dispatched) fc8ec3f
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE fc8ec3f
@tester-api APPROVE early tree; verified a 0-byte diff under src/main/, no API surface changed since

./mvnw verify → BUILD SUCCESS, 1236 tests / 0 failures, SpotBugs 0, Checkstyle 0, JaCoCo 96% instruction / 88% branch.

The evidence was re-derived, not transcribed

I rebuilt the verification harness against the project's own resolved test classpath rather than copying the review transcripts. The ticket's claim of 21 encodings was correct — the transcript had enumerated only 20 (the missing row is contexts: local,other). 13 leak, 8 suppress, and the leaking set is exactly the set that names nothing.

One finding sharper than the transcript: there are three discard points, not two, partitioning the 13 leaking rows as 8 + 4 + 1 — Boot's CollectionUtils.isEmpty → ifne, Liquibase's trimToNull → ifnonnull, and splitAndTrim(",", ",") returning empty. All three confirmed by javap.

Beyond the ticket's scope, because review demanded it

AC3's guard turned out not to be enough: nothing enforced the decision itself. @security-auditor graded that a MEDIUM — silent, fail-open and invisible at startup — so the story also ships `LiquibaseContextGatingAbsentTest` (org.maglez.eop.config, 5 tests), mutation-proven to fail on context=, contextFilter=, labels=, contexts: "" and contexts: no, and to fail closed on a missing or emptied changelog directory. Recorded in ADR-006 as a sixth class of build gate — configuration-absence tests — with an explicit admission test for the next one: the breach must be silent, fail-open and invisible at startup.

Four review rounds, three rejections — worth recording

@architecture-guardian rejected three times, each time on a real defect this story had itself introduced, and each of the same shape the story exists to eliminate — a checkable claim shipped alongside the instrument that disproves it:

  1. BLOCKER — the guard's matcher \bcontexts?\s*= could not match contextFilter=, which in liquibase-core 5.0.3 is the primary spelling (ChangeSet.java:432-434 reads it first; the XSD declares each 6×). Worse, the s? branch covered contexts=, declared zero times. The rule file had already promised agents the build would catch it.
  2. BLOCKER — ADR-043 asserted "1859 → 1112 bytes, a 40% cut" and printed the re-measurement command, which returned 1345. Self-refuted by the same commit that wrote it. Now stated as an invariant rather than a snapshot.
  3. MAJOR — the reduced rule entry still said "the spelling Liquibase 5 actually prefers", naming a library version and breaking AC1/AC4 while ADR-043 asserted the opposite in bold.

Also fixed en route: the rule file forbade context but never mentioned labels — the exact substitution ADR-043 predicts; ADR-008's Status line understated its amendment history; and ADR-043 claimed AdrIndexConsistencyTest makes any amendment visible, which this story disproved twice.

Accepted limitations, all gate-approved and conceded in the ADR

  • `contexts: {}` is invisible to the profile assertion — the flattener contributes no key at all, so no accessor can reach it. Backstopped by the changeset half.
  • Environment overrides (SPRING_LIQUIBASE_CONTEXTS=…) bypass the guard entirely and stay silent.
  • Four relaxed-binding spellings (label_filter:, LABEL-FILTER:, LABELFILTER:, CONTEXTS:) escape the property check — all fail closed.
  • `hasSizeGreaterThan(1)` is a weak anti-vacuity threshold; independently graded non-blocking by two gates.

Deferred items are filed as EOP-104, including the most valuable one: shouldCarryAmendmentDates cannot see an amendment that leaves the Status line untouched, and ADR-006's own amendment from this story is the live proof.

Delivered on branch eop-36-rule-file-fictions — PR #90 (https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/90). ./mvnw verify green: exit 0, 1236 tests, 0 failures. All five Definition-of-Done gates approved.

Two acceptance criteria were deliberately inverted, because verification falsified them. Flagging this prominently rather than burying it:

  • AC3 ("describe the scheme actually used") — the ticket names three shipped changelogs. There are nine, and both naming schemes are live: six NNN- files and three dated. Documenting both as equally valid would have been accurate and dangerous, because <includeAll> orders by filename with no manifest, so a 007- file — the obvious next step for anyone reading the legacy six as a live sequence — executes ahead of every dated migration, on a fresh database, with a green build everywhere already migrated past it. Confirmed empirically from the Liquibase log rather than assumed. So the dated scheme is declared the forward convention and NNN- is frozen at 006-. The legacy six cannot be renamed to unify the schemes: a filename is part of changeset identity, so renaming orphans DATABASECHANGELOG rows on every non-fresh environment. The split is permanent.
  • AC4 ("describe id numbering as global across files, as actually practised") — false as written. Eight of the nine files restart at 001; 002-real-deck.xml is the sole outlier. Implementing AC4 would have made the rule wrong for eight files in order to fix one — this ticket's own defect class, inverted, inside the very passage the ticket exists to de-fiction. The per-file rule is kept and the outlier named as unrenumberable legacy.

A third, unticketed fiction was found in the same passage and is fixed under AC5: the rule quoted <includeAll path="classpath:db/changelog/changes/"/>, an absolute form this repository does not use and which previously resolved to zero changesets in silence. An agent copying it would have reintroduced a migration setup that reports success and applies nothing. A fourth was removed in passing — the section's worked example named 2026-07-26--create-threat-card-table.xml, a file that never existed.

Part A resolved as option 2 (disclosure), and the evidence is stronger than the ticket's. Beyond the absent dependency: there is no RestTemplate, WebClient, RestClient, HttpClient or Feign client anywhere in src/main/java/, so Resilience4j — which wraps calls that leave the process — has nothing to wrap. Adoption would be pure supply-chain surface. The security gate added that @TimeLimiter cancels the wrapper rather than the in-flight JDBC statement, so bolting it onto the database path would create false assurance rather than a control. The "externalised per profile" fiction the ticket warned about is also fixed.

Scope discipline honoured. No enforcement test was added for the 007- freeze — the ticket's own warning that added scope "buys a fourth round rather than a better repo" was treated as binding. The security gate independently verified the hazard is fail-closed (Liquibase raises a missing-object error and the app refuses to start, the opposite direction from EOP-35's inert context="prod") and cannot reach the 004/005 constraint invariants, since 007- sorts after both. Recorded as the first negative consequence in ADR-044.

ADR-044 holds the ordering proof, the frozen-identity argument and the classpath: history; the rule file keeps only the directive and a one-line reason, per the placement precedent ADR-043 set in EOP-35. No ADR was written for Part A — declining a library never held closes no option and would produce a decision-shaped document with an empty Consequences section; the deferral already lives in CHANGELOG's "Decided, not yet implemented", and the rule now places the ADR gate at the moment adoption actually happens.

Five review findings were remediated in-story rather than deferred, each of them this story's own defect class turned on itself: a bare pom.xml:56 citation in a hot-path rule file (the rot vector that invalidated ADR-023's *Amends: citations in EOP-93); ADR-044 justifying the absent guard on an allow-list that "would go stale" when the freeze makes it a constant; docs/devops/local-development.md found to be an unlinked *second prescription of the scheme; a CHANGELOG paragraph that both made and disowned the same citation; and a hard-coded "three dated migrations" count the next migration would falsify.

Gate verdicts: @tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE (verified DeckArithmeticClaimsTest is safe by design, not by accident) · @tester-api APPROVE (independently falsified both codebase claims; 119 integration tests green) · @security-auditor APPROVE (three INFO findings, all pre-existing) · @code-reviewer APPROVE (every factual claim verified individually) · @architecture-guardian APPROVE (re-confirmed on the amended tree, having re-run verify itself).

Delivered on branch eop-38-secure-config-default — commits 489df50 and 8ead665. All five DoD gates approved. ./mvnw clean verify green (1272 tests, 0 failures).

Decision: Option A (invert the overlay), narrowed to springdoc

springdoc.api-docs.enabled: false and springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled: false moved from application-prod.yml into base application.yml. Local developers opt back in with SPRINGDOC_APIDOCS_ENABLED=true / SPRINGDOC_SWAGGERUI_ENABLED=true, added to .env.example and exported by .envrc's dotenv. application-prod.yml keeps its block as a deliberate redundant second guard. Recorded in ADR-048.

Option B (refuse to boot insecurely) was rejected for four reasons, argued in the ADR. Chiefly: its assertion would be dead code. The deployable jar already cannot boot on the default profile — java -jar exits 1 with IllegalStateException: Cannot load driver class: org.h2.Driver, because ADR-047 excludes H2 from the repackaged jar. It would also need a brittle "looks like a real deployment" heuristic that must not fire on a developer machine.

Two corrections to this ticket's premise, both measured

1. The stack-trace claim is false. The ticket states that omitting the profile yields "full stack traces in error responses". It does not. Every error path returns RFC 9457 with exactly detail, instance, status, title — no trace, no exception, no errors. /error returns {{

{"timestamp":…,"status":999,"error":"None"}

}}. So server.error.include-stacktrace: never and its three siblings in application-prod.yml are redundant pins of Spring Boot's own defaults (Boot 2.3+), not the source of any asymmetry — and the project bypasses BasicErrorController almost entirely via its RFC 9457 @ControllerAdvice. Independently reproduced by @tester-api and @security-auditor. The real fail-open surface was springdoc alone — one surface, not three.

2. The guarantee rested on one mechanism, not two. I hypothesised that {{spring.datasource.url: $

{DB_URL}

}} would also fail placeholder resolution, since compose.app.yml has no env_file: and the container never sees DB_URL. Disproven by experiment: with every DB_ and DATASOURCE_ variable unset, the failure was still the driver class, because DataSourceProperties.determineDriverClassName runs before the URL is used. So the sole guard was ADR-047's <excludes> block — whose stated purpose is artifact hygiene, not profile safety, and which per pom.xml:130-135 silently stops working if that execution's id is renamed from repackage (Maven merges executions by id; a rename yields a second execution while the inherited one runs without the exclusion, and the build stays green). That is why AC-2 needed a real answer rather than "already fine".

Acceptance criteria

AC Status
1 — deliberate decision recorded in an ADR ADR-048, both options weighed, Option B rejection argued
2 — no schema/UI/stack traces, or refuses to start Default profile: 404 on /v3/api-docs, /swagger-ui/index.html, /swagger-ui.html
3 — a test pins it, in H2ConsoleAbsentIntegrationTest style Two tests, mutation-verified
4 — SETUP.md accepted-risk register updated Rewritten; the risk is declared resolved, not accepted
5 — dated amendment if ADR-012's rationale is weakened Amended 2026-08-22 with matching docs/adr/README.md date

On AC-5: ADR-012's byte-identical rationale concerns not adding a third overlay profile. The profile count remains two, so that rationale survives intact — only its narrower lines 147-150 claim about Swagger UI being locally available by default needed qualifying. ADR-047's revisit trigger is not tripped: the default profile gains no deployed role. Both points were checked by @architecture-guardian as a gate rather than taken on trust.

Measured evidence

  /v3/api-docs Swagger UI /health
Before 200, 18,739 bytes 200 200
After, no opt-in 404, 103 bytes 404 200
After, opt-in set 200, 18,739 bytes 200 200

Both limbs proven: the control is effective and satisfiable. The second matters — per ADR-047's precedent, "a ban with no sanctioned escape hatch trains people to disable bans". SpringdocOptInIntegrationTest exists so "disabled" can never be satisfied by springdoc merely being broken.

Mutation test: flipping the base back to true gives Tests run: 4, Failures: 3, with the positive control correctly still passing.

Defense in depth

Three independent mechanisms now guard this surface, where there was one: base configuration (application.yml), the profile overlay (application-prod.yml, which wins over an injected env var), and the artifact layer (ADR-047's <excludes>).

Residual, recorded in ADR-048

Two SPRINGDOC_* variables now exist that could in principle be set in a deployed environment. Mitigated — not prevented — by prod's second guard and by compose.app.yml having no env_file:. A developer who never copies .env.example loses local Swagger UI until they do.

Branch eop-40-frontend-scaffolded-truth, four commits: ff44808 → 458d3fe → fcd521f → efb1b8d. Six files, 104 insertions / 12 deletions, all Markdown — no production or test code.

Acceptance criteria

AC 1 — met. The AGENTS.md Front-end bullet now opens "Front-end: shipped, not pending." and covers Stack, Location, Build and Serving. Note the "not scaffolded yet" wording quoted in this ticket had already been partly cleaned up before I started; what was still missing was build and serving, and any citation more precise than "see CHANGELOG.md".

AC 2 — met. Every claim cites a tracked path. @code-reviewer verified all 22 individually against the filesystem.

AC 3 — met, and the ADR diverged in five places, not the one this ticket anticipated:

  1. React 19 → ui/package.json pins react ^18.3.1
  2. A src/ tree of components/ pages/ hooks/ services/ types/ plus public/ → only components/ was ever built; the real tree also has assets/ and utils/
  3. Dev server `:5173` → ui/vite.config.ts sets 5371, proxying /api and /health
  4. DTOs in `ui/src/types/` → they live in ui/src/api.ts, hand-maintained, not generated from docs/api/openapi.yml
  5. A promised `GovUkPage` component → never built; its five items are split across two files (<head> and skip link in ui/index.html, header/footer/main inline in ui/src/App.tsx)

Recorded as a dated ## Amendments section with a five-row evidence table, plus five inline pointers at the stale sites. Original decision text preserved as historical record, per the ADR-002/006/008 house convention.

AC 4 — met. docs/adr/README.md's Implemented? cell is byte-identical — @architecture-guardian proved it by hashing the pipe field on both sides (3b8719ff…, unchanged across all four commits). Only the Status cell moved, Accepted → Accepted (amended 2026-08-19), and that edit is forced by AdrIndexConsistencyTest.shouldCarryAmendmentDates: once the ADR's status line carries an ISO date, the index cell must repeat it or the build fails. @tester-unit-and-quality confirmed that guard would genuinely have failed on a bare Accepted — not a vacuous pass. That is a build-gate justification, which is what AC 4 permits.

Two things found beyond the brief

A fifth copy of the corrected claims, in the file that acts on them. .opencode/agents/ui-builder.md — the definition of the only agent that writes React — told it to use React 19, to Import shared types from ../types/, and to put fetch wrappers under src/services/. Two of those are imperatives: a UI story dispatched there would have been instructed to recreate the very directories this ticket documents as never built. Found by @architecture-guardian, which rejected the branch over it. Fixing the ADR and leaving that standing would have closed this finding on paper only.

The last live instance of the original falsehood was docs/devops/local-development.md:5 ("…the React front-end (ADR-009), which is not scaffolded yet"), in a file that contradicted itself 173 lines later. Also corrected there: the Node floor, which said 20+ where ui/package.json requires 22 — and @security-auditor established from the Node release schedule that 20 reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30, so the document was recommending an unpatched runtime.

Definition of Done — five approvals, all on the final commit

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE

Not first time. @architecture-guardian rejected the branch and was right to — besides the agent brief above, it caught my own amendment asserting ui/src/App.tsx carries govuk-skip-link when the skip link is at ui/index.html:14. That is this ticket's defect class, reproduced inside the Evidence column of the correction. Three remediation rounds followed, each re-verified. ./mvnw verify → BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 1236, Failures: 0, coverage met, independently re-run by three gates.

Follow-ups raised

  • EOP-105 — a genuine production defect found by @tester-api: ui/src/api.ts declares role: 'PLAYER' and status: 'ENDED', neither of which the server ever emits, and omits PARTICIPANT, COMPLETED and ABANDONED, which it does. Confirmed against PlayerRole.java and SessionStatus.java, not just the OpenAPI spec. Every comparison against those values is silently dead code. This is exactly the drift ADR-009's new amendment warns is possible in a hand-maintained mirror — it had already happened.
  • EOP-106 — whether ui/vite.config.ts's port: 5371 is deliberate or a transposition of Vite's 5173. Documented as-is here because code is authoritative for behaviour; @architecture-guardian specifically endorsed not writing an ADR to rationalise it.
  • EOP-107 — front-end security hardening, five non-blocking items from @security-auditor plus the UI builder brief's missing security section.

Two accepted-but-open nits, both raised by a reviewer that then approved: ADR-009's ### The shipped layout says "no public/" without noting that ui/public/ is generated by the prebuild script and gitignored (true as written of the tracked tree, and the frame is unstated); and @tester-unit-and-quality now recommends a build-time guard pinning the agent-brief claims, having reversed its earlier position after two gates each found a further false claim introduced by a fix. Both are one-line changes deliberately left out of a story that had already taken three remediation rounds.

Resolved. Implementation landed in PR #91 (merge 7d86b64, branch eop-40-frontend-scaffolded-truth) and is on main. Docs-only — @security-auditor confirmed the merge touched no production source, so the attack surface of this change is zero.

Acceptance criteria

AC Result
AGENTS.md describes the front end as shipped (stack, location, build, serving) PASS — grep "not scaffolded" AGENTS.md returns nothing. The bullet now covers stack, location, build and serving
Every claim verifiable against a tracked file cited by path PASS — verified against ui/package.json: engines.node >= 22.12 (L8), govuk-frontend ^5.7.1 (L23), react ^18.3.1 (L24), typescript ^5.6.3 (L40), vite ^7.3.6 (L42). Matches AGENTS.md exactly — including that React is 18, not the 19 ADR-009 claimed

ADR-009's status line (L3) records six amendments (four on 2026-08-19, two on 2026-08-20) with inline boxes at L44 (React major wrong), L59 (directory tree aspirational; entry document is ui/index.html at package root), L80, L88, L94 (contract anchor is the module ui/src/api.ts, not a directory), each tagged (EOP-40)
docs/adr/README.md unchanged PASS with one correction to the AC's wording — see below

On the "README.md unchanged" criterion

@code-reviewer established that commit ff44808 did touch docs/adr/README.md, in exactly one way: the ADR-009 row's status cell went Accepted → Accepted (amended 2026-08-19).

That is not the regression the AC was guarding against. The AC existed because this ticket inverted an earlier finding — @code-reviewer had read AGENTS.md as authoritative and logged that the ADR index row was wrong; @architecture-guardian checked the filesystem and established the reverse. The index's substance was correct and was not altered. Recording an amendment date in the index is mandatory bookkeeping: AdrIndexConsistencyTest.shouldCarryAmendmentDates requires every ISO date in an ADR's status line to appear in its index cell, so omitting that edit would have turned the build red.

Worth preserving for future readers: the filesystem beat the documentation here. When AGENTS.md and a tracked file disagree, check the file.

Build evidence

  • ./mvnw clean verify → exit 0, BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 1256, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
  • ui/ npm run verify → exit 0, Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 223 passed (223), production build succeeded

Gate verdicts — all five APPROVE

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE

Accepted-but-open — and one premise I had wrong

I briefed both reviewing gates that ADR-009's inline amendment box at L80 still asserted :5371 with the supersession recorded only in the status line. @architecture-guardian refused to ratify that and was right to. The dated supersession is inside the same blockquote at ADR-009:84-88 ("Superseded by EOP-106 (2026-08-20): the port is `:5173` again."), the second site at :213 is superseded immediately below at :215-222 with commit forensics (7efd900 EOP-9 Done created it correctly at 5173; 496d7b5 EOP-63 To Do mistyped it; author confirmed "I had no reason for changing the port number"), and the amendment-table row at :158 carries its own inline supersession.

The genuine residue is narrower: the section heading text at ADR-009:213 still reads `{{### Why the front-end port is }}:5371{{ }}`. A supersession blockquote cannot reach a heading — and headings are what a reader scans, what a TOC lists, and what an anchor exposes.

Attributed to EOP-106, not this ticket: EOP-40's amendment was correct when written; EOP-106 reverted the code and superseded it. No ticket opened — ADR-009:820 documents the in-place-supersession convention deliberately, every reading path reaches a dated retraction within two lines, and rewriting the heading would break the anchor and erase the history the convention exists to keep. Fold it into the next ADR-009 amendment.

Also noted, informational: ADR-009:766 claims "1244 tests" and "all four documentation-integrity gates". Now 1,256 tests and five classes in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ — drift caused by EOP-120, out of scope here, and no guard watches counted claims in prose.

EOP-48.renderedBody:
Delivered and merged to main via PR #52 (merge commit 31458cb).

What was wrong

SessionController's @ConditionalOnProperty omitted havingValue. Verified against the resolved spring-boot-autoconfigure-4.1.0 bytecode rather than the documentation: with havingValue empty, OnPropertyCondition$Spec.isMatch reduces to !"false".equalsIgnoreCase(value). So off, no, 0, disabled — and the empty string, which is what EOP_FEATURES_SESSION_LIFECYCLE= produces and which was recorded nowhere before this ticket — all enabled the five session routes. off is the worst of them: it is both the spelling an operator reaches for as a kill switch and a YAML 1.1 boolean false, so it would have passed review unremarked.

matchIfMissing already defaults to false, so an absent property was never the hole. The hole was confined to the present-but-not-false case.

The controller was only the symptom. The four session use-case beans in UseCaseConfiguration were registered unconditionally, so a misspelt flag had nothing to fail against — which is why this differed from TrickController, corrected in 56c31b1, and why it needed its own ticket rather than a one-line follow-up.

What changed

`34d30d7` — EOP-48 Done fix: close fail-open @ConditionalOnProperty on the session lifecycle flag

  • SessionController.java:60 now carries havingValue = "true".
  • createSessionUseCase (:101), joinSessionUseCase (:124), getSessionStateUseCase (:167) and startSessionUseCase (:182) each carry @ConditionalOnProperty(name = "eop.features.session-lifecycle", havingValue = "true").
  • resolvePlayerUseCase deliberately ungated, with the reason in javadoc: pure read (verified — no save/persist/delete anywhere in it), and shared with all five trick-play use cases, so gating it on the lobby flag would make lobby-off/trick-play-on an unsatisfiable context. Eight consumers traced: two lifecycle, five trick-play, plus the controller.
  • New SessionLifecycleOffValueIntegrationTest (12 tests) pinning the off spelling: five bean-absence assertions, five route 404s, one counterweight asserting ResolvePlayerUseCase and PlayCardUseCase survive, one asserting /api/v1/cards still answers 200.

`50850d1` — EOP-48 Done docs: correct the five documents that still described the fail-open flag

The review found five stale documents, not the two the brief named: ADR-013 (predecessor count, three now-false clauses kept and marked spent because an ADR is a record, plus a dated note carrying the full mechanism and a strengthened mandate), ADR-028 (predecessor discharged, two of three remain), docs/adr/README.md (Implemented column only, so AdrIndexConsistencyTest stays green), docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md (its annotation quote had itself omitted havingValue, and it carried a live paragraph describing the hole as unfixed), and src/main/resources/application.yml (both flag comments — ADR-028:76-77 designates the trick-play one part of the predecessor register).

ADR-013's mandate is now two sentences rather than one: every @ConditionalOnProperty on a flag carries havingValue = "true", and the flag is repeated on every bean that opens or mutates the state behind it — pure reads and cross-flag collaborators staying ungated with the reason in javadoc.

The fix was measured, not asserted

Against the pre-fix code the new test fails 6 of 12: the five bean-absence assertions plus exactly one route — POST /api/v1/sessions returning 201 Created and persisting a session with the flag set to off. The other four routes return 404 either way, because a random session id and an unissued join code are absent whether or not the controller exists.

That is the argument for asserting bean absence alongside the 404s: a status-only test would have caught this on one route in five, and only because that route creates something. A read-only lobby would have been missed entirely. SessionControllerDisabledIntegrationTest (spelling false) is byte-identical and passed both before and after — only a second spelling could catch this.

Post-fix, exactly one value enables the feature: case-insensitive true. Absent, empty and every other spelling fail closed. All eleven @ConditionalOnProperty sites in src/main/ now carry havingValue = "true"; zero loose forms remain.

Acceptance criteria

Criterion Status
SessionController carries havingValue = "true" ✅ :60
Four session use-case beans gated ✅ :101, :124, :167, :182
resolvePlayerUseCase remains ungated ✅ with javadoc, plus a test asserting it present in the off context
New scenario with session-lifecycle=off asserting bean absence, not merely 404s ✅ SessionLifecycleOffValueIntegrationTest, 12 tests
Existing SessionControllerDisabledIntegrationTest passes unchanged ✅ byte-identical, 7/7
./mvnw verify green ✅ 905 tests, 0 failures; checkstyle 0, spotbugs 0, jacoco met, enforcer 3/3

Definition of Done — five gates, five approvals

Every gate ran ./mvnw verify itself rather than taking the build on trust.

  • @tester-unit-and-quality — APPROVE. Decompiled OnPropertyCondition$Spec to confirm the pre-fix behaviour. SessionController 100% (105/105), UseCaseConfiguration 100% (96/96), bundle 97.3%. Argued off alone is sufficient — pinning no/0/disabled would test Spring, not the application, at three more Spring contexts.
  • @tester-api — APPROVE. Confirmed the 404s are the framework's own NoResourceFoundException, not a GlobalExceptionHandler mapping and not a masked 403. Confirmed no residual write path: SessionRepositoryAdapter exists unconditionally but has no reachable caller. `docs/api/openapi.yml:44-47` already stated the gate and the 404 behaviour, so the contract needed no change — the bug was the implementation not honouring it.
  • @security-auditor — APPROVE, no CRITICAL or HIGH. Proved the mechanism against bytecode and found the previously unrecorded empty-string case. Confirmed no join code, token hash or session envelope leaks through the ungated path. Argued against adding startup validation of eop.features.*: the remaining failure modes (on/yes/1, a misspelt key) all fail closed and are loud, a validator would turn an operability annoyance into a boot crash, and it would need a second register that can drift.
  • @code-reviewer — APPROVE, zero blockers. Zero Spring imports in usecase/ and entity/. The two annotation spellings (prefix+name on controllers, dotted name on beans) judged each idiomatic in context, explicitly not a finding.
  • @architecture-guardian — APPROVE. The agent that regraded this HIGH and made it a condition of approving Slice D. Judged the two-layer gate genuine defence in depth on the axis that matters: remove havingValue from the controller tomorrow and the context fails to start rather than failing open, because the constructor requires four beans that no longer exist. Authored the four document corrections.

CI on the PR: build, ui and image all green (run 31828428083).

Follow-ups filed rather than smuggled in

  • An automated check that every @ConditionalOnProperty in src/main carries havingValue = "true". The mandate was already in ADR-013 and has now been violated twice, so reviewer attention has demonstrably not been enough. Deliberately not done here: the tool choice (ArchUnit vs a docs-style test in the manner of AdrIndexConsistencyTest) is a new decision needing its own ADR, and that does not belong in a fix commit.
  • EOP-25's description needs amending before that flip is attempted — most importantly because only the literal true now flips the flag, so on/yes/1 are silent no-ops. That inversion is the deliberate price of failing closed and belongs in the ticket that performs the flip.

Notes for the record

  • Exposure was latent, not live: application.yml has always shipped session-lifecycle: false, which was one of the six letters that did work.
  • This ticket's own description cites SessionController.java:51; the annotation is at :60. Same citation-drift class as EOP-49.
  • EOP-48 is discharged as a predecessor of EOP-25 and of the story that flips trick-play on (ADR-028), which now has two of its three predecessors outstanding.

EOP-50.renderedBody:
*Delivered on PR 118(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/118)* — branch eop-50-having-value-build-enforcement, three commits (322455d → a03a522 → a4a4462), awaiting human approval.

Acceptance criteria

Criterion Status
An ADR exists recording the decision, the alternatives, and the trade-off accepted ✅ ADR-052, all four alternatives weighed
A build-failing check asserts every @ConditionalOnProperty in src/main/ carries havingValue = "true" ✅ ConditionalOnPropertyHavingValueTest
The check is proven to fail, with the actual output recorded in the PR ✅ three deliberately loosened sites, verbatim output in the PR body
.opencode/rules/feature-flags.md carries the rule ✅ inserted as bullet 2, your verbatim wording plus the enforcement asymmetry
If bean-level repetition is not mechanically checkable, the ADR says so and why ✅ ADR-052 states it openly, with the three reasons
./mvnw verify green ✅ BUILD SUCCESS, 1289 tests, 0 failures

Mechanism

Spring's own ASM metadata reader (SimpleMetadataReaderFactory over a FileSystemResource per .class file, walking target/classes with Files.walk) — zero new dependencies, since spring-core is already on the test classpath. Because it reads bytecode rather than source text, annotation defaults are applied: an omitted havingValue reads back as "" and is caught by the same positive comparison against "true", and no formatting, attribute order or line wrapping can defeat it. This is what sank the docs-style text-parsing alternative. ArchUnit was a close call, rejected as a new dependency for what spring-core already does, and noted in the ADR as the natural upgrade if a second architectural invariant ever needs enforcing.

Two corrections to the ticket's own framing

  1. The "eleven sites" baseline is stale. There are 21 on origin/main (6 class-level + 15 method-level in UseCaseConfiguration), across three flags — trick-play and game-over both landed after this ticket was filed on 2026-08-14. All 21 already comply, so the gate is preventive: it fixes no live defect and locks in a property the code already has.
  2. A second invariant was added during this story's own review round. @security-auditor rejected the first implementation with a BLOCKER: a site written havingValue = "true", matchIfMissing = true satisfies the ADR-013 mandate to the letter while enabling the feature whenever the property is absent — inverting the fail-closed default, and needing no operator action at all to fire, which is worse in that one respect than a loose havingValue. This does not contradict EOP-48's finding that matchIfMissing "already defaults false"; it qualifies it to the loose form, since a default is not a prohibition and a later commit can override one. The gate now asserts both invariants separately, and their independence was verified empirically — loosening matchIfMissing fails 1 of 4 tests, leaving the havingValue assertion passing.

On @architecture-guardian's MAJOR, the prohibition is recorded in ADR-013 (dated 2026-08-23 amendment) rather than ADR-052, so the whole flag mandate reads in one place; ADR-052 owns the mechanism for both invariants.

Out of scope, as the ticket directed

Startup validation of eop.features.* values was *not implemented. @security-auditor's EOP-48 reasoning was respected, not relitigated.

Honest limits

  • The gate is preventive, not corrective.
  • Only the first half of the strengthened ADR-013 mandate is mechanised. Bean-level repetition remains reviewer-enforced — @architecture-guardian agreed it is not mechanically checkable: "opens or mutates the flagged state" is a semantic judgement no signature encodes, the carve-outs are justified in unparseable javadoc prose, and mechanising it would recreate the drift-prone per-flag bean register that EOP-48's security analysis rejected.
  • No src/main/ file was touched.

Definition of Done — five gates, all VERDICT: APPROVE

@tester-unit-and-quality · @tester-api · @security-auditor (approved on re-dispatch, BLOCKER closed) · @code-reviewer (Warning closed) · @architecture-guardian (MAJOR closed). Both above-NIT findings were remediated and the raising agents re-dispatched, rather than downgraded to caveats.

EOP-56.renderedBody:
Delivered in PR #116 (branch eop-56-503-log-level-justification, commit c2e9c8b). Two corrections to this ticket are worth recording before the summary, because both would cause harm if copied forward.

1. Three of the four acceptance criteria were already met when this ticket was written

The rate limit shipped under EOP-19 (commit 963a10b, 2026-08-15), which this ticket does not reference. That commit added SessionCreationLimiter (port), InMemorySessionCreationLimiter (sliding window, 5 creations per address per 60s, fail-closed on saturation), RateLimitedException → 429, and ADR-033.

So against the stated Definition of Done:

Criterion Status
The create path is rate-limited Already done — EOP-19
A test asserts the limit fires Already done — 19 unit tests in InMemorySessionCreationLimiterTest, plus SessionControllerIntegrationTest.ThrottlingCreation asserting 429 + Retry-After
The 503's log-level justification cites the control Delivered here
./mvnw verify green Delivered here — 1285 tests, 0 failures

The ticket also said the success-vs-failure counting policy "deserves its own ADR paragraph". ADR-033 already carries it, under the heading "Why successes are counted, not failures."

The premise in the ticket body — that `CreateSessionUseCase` has no limiter, so anonymous callers create lobbies at full rate — was already false when the ticket was filed. Worth knowing for any sibling ticket raised in the same review pass.

2. The ticket's arithmetic understates the keyspace by a factor of 1024

The body states the collision probability as roughly (N / 2^30)^5. The exponent is right; the base is not.

JoinCode.ALPHABET is 32 characters (Crockford base32) and JoinCode.LENGTH is 8, so the code space is 32⁸ = *2⁴⁰* = 1,099,511,627,776 — forty bits, not thirty. The correct expression is (N / 2^40)^5. ADR-019's "finite and forty bits wide" was always correct.

This matters beyond pedantry: thirty bits was the superseded six-character width, retired by EOP-24 precisely because it was enumerable by a distributed attacker. Quoting 2^30 as current reads as though that decision had never been taken. The figure is now derived from the constants by a build gate rather than restated, so the ticket's version cannot be copied back in.

What shipped

The justification now rests on a control. SessionController consults the limiter before CreateSessionUseCase.execute, so every request reaching the join-code retry loop has already passed it. The rate at which the WARN-with-stack-trace can be driven is bounded by the configured per-address allowance and by the limiter's 10,000-key ceiling, which fails closed on an unrecognised address. The arithmetic is why an occurrence is evidence worth logging; the limiter is why it cannot become a flood, and it is the half that survives a change to the attempt budget, the alphabet or the code length — which is exactly the fragility this ticket raised.

A build gate keeps the arithmetic honest. JoinCodeSpaceClaimsTest derives the width from the two constants and fails if a live claim stops quoting it, over two layers: three phrase-anchored checks on the sentences whose argument depends on the figure, and a sweep of every .java, .md and .yml file under src/main/java, docs/architecture, docs/adr and docs/api, requiring each English-word bit figure to equal the derived width or sit on a seven-entry allowlist of deliberately historical mentions that fails in both directions. With LENGTH temporarily set to 7 it enumerates 27 stale sites — the hand-audit EOP-24 performed, now printed by the build.

Changed: GlobalExceptionHandler (Javadoc only), docs/adr/ADR-019-session-lifecycle-and-join-codes.md (new dated amendment), CHANGELOG.md, and the new test. No behaviour changed — status, Retry-After and log level are as EOP-17 left them.

Limits, stated rather than implied

  • The gate pins two of three constants. MAXIMUM_CODE_ATTEMPTS is private to CreateSessionUseCase and reachable only by reflection, so the attempt budget stays a reviewer's concern.
  • It verifies that prose and constants agree, never that forty bits is adequate. That judgement stays in ADR-019.
  • It reads English number words only, so 2^40 or 40 bits passes unexamined, and the allowlist is keyed on filename plus number word rather than on a passage — so a file legitimately quoting the superseded "thirty bits" would also tolerate a second, genuinely stale mention beside it. Narrowing that key is the named next move.
  • The limiter is keyed per address while the occupied fraction of the code space is global, so it bounds the rate of this log line and not the number of live lobbies. Stated in the ADR rather than collapsed.

Review

All five Definition-of-Done gates approved the shipping tree. Two findings changed the work materially rather than being noted and waved through: @tester-api found that docs/api/openapi.yml states the width three times and sat outside the sweep's roots — closed rather than deferred, since a contract is what a client integrates against — and @code-reviewer rejected an earlier revision over four blockers, including a miscount in the very prose announcing this fix. Both are recorded in ADR-019 and the changelog rather than quietly corrected.

This ticket blocks EOP-25, which is already Done, so no downstream work is waiting on it.

Resolved — the reported defect was already fixed; this ticket delivered the nomenclature alignment

The symptom this ticket reports is not present on `main`, and has not been since `35c3ed0` (EOP-70). That commit added both halves of the fix this ticket prescribes, in one go:

  • ui/src/api.ts gained the deal helper calling {{POST /api/v1/sessions/ {sessionId}

    /deal}}

  • LobbyScreen.handleStartGame gained the await call to it, immediately after startGame() succeeds

It was already covered by three tests in ui/src/components/LobbyScreen.test.tsx and ui/src/api.test.ts — success path, failure path and call count — all of which stub global fetch rather than spying on the module, so the ADR-045 boundary parsers are genuinely exercised.

The residual timing window is benign and tested: the SSE game-started event can mount GameScreen while the deal request is still in flight, but GameScreen absorbs the resulting 409 (HandNotDealtException) as a waiting state, and the subsequent hand-dealt event triggers a re-fetch that populates the hand. A lost race therefore degrades to "waiting", not to "Could not load game".

What this ticket did deliver

What EOP-70 did not do was agree on a name. docs/api/openapi.yml:475 declares operationId: dealHands, and both TrickController.dealHands and DealHandsUseCase carry it — three of four layers said dealHands and only the browser said dealCards. The divergence is exactly the kind that defeats grep-based archaeology, and it is what produced the wrong initial diagnosis on this very ticket.

Commit `e648cd7` — "[EOP-67] refactor: rename dealCards to dealHands to match operationId", merged to main as b6e8447 via PR #107. Eight files, +26 / −22:

  • Helper, import, call site and both Vitest suites renamed. Function body byte-identical — same route, same POST, same player-token header, still 204, still correctly parser-free per .opencode/rules/error-handling.md
  • Live prose updated in three documents: ADR-045 §4's parser roster, ADR-040's non-atomic start-then-deal limitation, and C4-Diagrams.md's parser-exemption paragraph

  • ADR-045's one historical mention deliberately keeps (then named dealCards — renamed by EOP-67) so a reader meeting the old name in git log has somewhere to land

No Java changed. No route, method, header, status code, response body or behaviour changed.

  • HandsTest pins 23/23/22, 17×4, 14/14/14/13/13 and 12/12/11/11/11/11 with every card dealt exactly once at every supported table size; DealHandsUseCaseTest pins totalCards() == 68 and 23 at the first seat.

The observed 22/22/22 = 66 is exactly `68 − (68 mod 3)` — the arithmetic signature of the equal-hands truncation EOP-72 introduced and EOP-92 reverted. The observation predates that revert.

Consequently the acceptance criterion "a test asserts the agreed deal distribution so the count cannot drift again" was already satisfied four times over, and no fifth pin was added. Adding one would have been duplicate coverage presented as a fix.

Divergence 2 — real, but mislocated, and its second half is false

The leaderboard operation and GetLeaderboardUseCase never disagreed. What was wrong sat in the `Leaderboard` schema description, which claimed the leaderboard is "available in any session state, not only COMPLETED" — contradicting the operation description directly above it and the 409 guard. So the spec contradicted itself, not the code. The schema description was rewritten; the code was not touched.

The claim that "the 409 is absent from that operation's documented responses" is false, and was already false when the ticket was written. git show b6e8447:docs/api/openapi.yml shows a full inline '409' block with an application/problem+json body on that operation at the merge base. The one place the stale claim had propagated — a javadoc sentence in GameOverControllerIntegrationTest.Rfc9457ContractGuards saying the reconciliation "is tracked as EOP-83" — is corrected.

Net change

Documentation only — no production Java touched (CHANGELOG.md, docs/api/openapi.yml, and one test javadoc). ./mvnw clean verify green at 1266 tests.

One limit stated plainly: this does not decide whether the leaderboard should become available before completion. It records that today it is not, in both halves of the spec. If that behaviour is wanted, it is a two-sided change — LeaderboardDto.sessionStatus is one of EnumMirrorParityTest's four client-checked unions, so an ABANDONED value would raise ContractViolationError in the browser (ADR-045) — and it deserves its own ticket rather than being smuggled in here.

Implemented — PR 119(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/119), branch `eop-84-derived-feature-flag-registry`, 8 commits, awaiting human review and merge.

./mvnw verify → Tests run: 1347, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS, zero [ERROR] lines.

What changed

ShippedFeatureFlagDefaultsTest is deleted. FeatureFlagRegistryTest derives the flag set three independent ways and requires all three equal:

Source Mechanism
Shipped config keys under eop.features in application.yml, read as a ClassPathResource through YamlPropertiesFactoryBean, no Spring context
Compiled code every @ConditionalOnProperty in target/classes resolving into that namespace, via SimpleMetadataReaderFactory as ADR-052's scanner does
Declared intent entries in the new src/test/resources/feature-flag-registry.yml

Each pairing catches a different fault. A YAML key with no registry entry is an undeclared flag whose intended state nobody wrote down. An annotation key in neither the YAML nor the registry is the fail-closed trap itself — no declared default, so the flag ships OFF silently. An entry with neither is a stale or misspelled declaration describing protection that is not there.

The direction of the assertion is what changed. The old guard was silent unless someone remembered to add a line; this one fails until someone declares intent — the tripwire EOP-27 built, rather than a snapshot of today's three positions.

The registry declares key, shipped-default, owner-story and expiry, all four mandatory in both directions so shipped-defualt fails as a surplus field rather than reading as an absent shipped-default plus a harmless extra key. expiry may be null but may not be omitted — that is what stops a new flag inheriting no-expiry by silence. game-over carries the 2026-09-18 date ADR-042 wrote in prose, now enforced; the other two carry null, because ADR-042 condemned inventing dates no decision authorised.

Zero new dependencies — SnakeYAML was already compile-scope. git diff --stat e88b2c2..HEAD – src/main/java/ src/main/resources/ docs/api/openapi.yml is empty: no production code, shipped config or API contract changed.

Acceptance criteria — each demonstrated by deliberate mutation

Mutation Test that failed
new YAML key, no registry entry shouldAgreeBetweenShippedYamlAndRegistry
that key plus an entry, but no @ConditionalOnProperty shouldAgreeBetweenBytecodeAndRegistry
registry shipped-default: false while YAML says true shouldMatchShippedValueToDeclaredIntent
game-over expiry moved one day into the past shouldFailOnceAFlagPassesItsExpiry
expiry field omitted shouldRequireEveryFieldOnEveryEntry

Documentation: new ADR-053 + index row; ADR-042 amended (§3 superseded, both weakness bullets closed); ADR-013 amended; .opencode/rules/feature-flags.md reworded to except a machine-read build-gating registry from its "no separate flag catalogue document" prohibition; CHANGELOG.md.

Definition of Done — five of five approved on final HEAD

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE (one REJECT raised and cleared)
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE

Four rounds, not one. Five substantive faults were found by reviewers and fixed rather than shipped as caveats:

  1. A `shipped-default` typo read as a deliberate declaration. Boolean.TRUE.equals(raw) answered false for anything that was not the boolean true, so shipped-default: flase arrived as a String and read back as "this flag ships dark". Worse, the same typo in application.yml would have agreed with it, since Spring treats every value but the literal true as disabled — the pair would have passed the guard while the flag shipped OFF. The EOP-82 fault reintroduced through the mechanism built to catch it. Field values are now type-asserted, not coerced.
  2. The ADR-053 index row was inserted out of sequence (051, 053, 052), and AdrIndexConsistencyTest does not check row order — silent drift of exactly the kind this story exists to remove.
  3. `registryKeys()`'s javadoc promised declaration order while the code sorted. The sort was dropped rather than the javadoc amended, because declaration order points a reader at the line to edit and the other two derivations sort for a reason this one does not have.
  4. ADR-042 carried a false claim — that a suite staying green after an incomplete flag removal is the evidence of it. It goes red: the OFF-position test asserts bean absence, not merely that the routes 404. This mattered because it is the paragraph whoever removes game-over on 2026-09-19 reads first, and a reader expecting green who meets red may revert a correct change.
  5. That claim existed in three places, in three file types, and correcting it took three commits one round apart — the ADR, the expiry assertion message, and the registry comment (the last found by @tester-api, which rejected the commit before it). Each was found by a reviewer; none by the build.

One of my own claims was false and is corrected in the record: I repeated a round-1 assertion that the consistent-removal gap was already documented in ADR-053. It was not. It is now, in §5 and in Consequences.

Recorded as bounds, not glossed

  • owner-story and shipped-default are checked for shape and agreement, never for truth — nothing verifies EOP-25 is a real issue.
  • A consistent removal across all three sources is undetected. The vacuity floor is "at least one", not "exactly the three that exist today"; pinning the count would make the guard a snapshot again, and the count cannot be derived because all three sources are what is under suspicion.
  • `game-over`'s expiry will turn `main` red on 2026-09-19 in a project that deploys every passing commit — accepted as the intended signal, on the accepted-advisories.json precedent.
  • ADR-037's front-end VITE_ flags remain *entirely uncovered; a front-end feature can still ship dark.
  • The masking trap itself is untouched — flags stay pinned ON in test resources. ADR-053 routes around it rather than removing it.

@architecture-guardian ruled EOP-84 architecturally complete with no follow-up tickets required.

EOP-88.renderedBody:
Implemented on branch eop-88-read-route-rate-limiting. PR open for human review and merge: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/117

Acceptance criteria

AC Status Evidence
1. Documented configurable limit on read routes incl. GET /leaderboard Met ReadRateLimitProperties binds eop.web.read-rate-limit (limit: 300, max-tracked-keys: 10000); ReadRateLimitInterceptor registered by WebInterceptorConfiguration on GET/HEAD under /api/v1/**
2. 429 + RFC 9457 problem+json, unit-tested mapping and integration-tested body Met Mapping was already covered by GlobalExceptionHandlerTest before this story — verified, not rewritten. Body asserted by ReadRateLimitIntegrationTest incl. a Retry-After value matched against ^[1-9][0-9]*$
3. Limiter key cannot be influenced by any request header, explicit test Met Key is ClientAddressResolver.of(request). ReadRateLimitInterceptorTest has a 15-case nested class over twelve headers — X-Forwarded-For (including rotated per request), Forwarded, X-Real-IP, X-Client-IP, Client-IP, True-Client-IP, CF-Connecting-IP, X-Cluster-Client-IP, X-Originating-IP, X-Remote-Addr, X-Forwarded, and X-EoP-Player-Token. server.forward-headers-strategy: none is the second independent guard
4. Test isolation does not forge the limiter key Met Suite-wide raised limit in src/test/resources/application.properties, plus @SpringBootTest(properties = "eop.web.read-rate-limit.limit=3") and @DirtiesContext per class. No test sends a forwarding header
5. ADR records the layer and the rejected alternatives Met [ADR-051|docs/adr/ADR-051-read-route-rate-limit.md] — interceptor chosen; servlet filter, Caddy plugin and per-controller checks each rejected with reasons, plus ten accepted limitations

Terminology correction

The ticket says "authenticated read routes". ADR-015 records that there is no authentication in this application — the routes carry an X-EoP-Player-Token capability and answer 403 without one. The ADR and the code say token-bearing instead.

Why the key is an address and not the player token

The counter must fail closed when its key table saturates (ADR-033). A token is client-supplied and unvalidated at the interceptor layer, so keying on it would let one caller mint 10,000 bogus tokens, fill the table, and have the limiter refuse everybody. A spoofable identifier must not select the bucket a fail-closed control counts in.

Definition of Done — all five gates approved

@tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer and @architecture-guardian all returned VERDICT: APPROVE. The first two rejected initially; commit a1072f6 closed their findings and both re-approved.

Two findings were substantive and are worth recording here:

  • `ProblemDetail.type` was documented as required but is never sent. RFC 9457 §3.1 makes the member optional with a default of about:blank, and Spring omits it while it holds that default. docs/api/openapi.yml listed it in required — a claim no response in this API has ever satisfied. Corrected to required: [title, status]. Pre-existing and affecting every 4xx/5xx response, in scope here only because this story added seven new references to TooManyRequests.
  • *`GET /api/v1/sessions/ {id}

    /events` answers 404, not 403, for an unknown session* — it checks session existence before resolving the player, unlike /leaderboard. The integration test now pins that status.

Known limitations, recorded rather than hidden

SSE reconnection is not rate limited — preHandle runs again on the ASYNC dispatch, so a naive counter would double-count every stream; its cost is bounded by the ADR-034 subscriber cap instead. Counters are in memory and per-instance (ADR-012). NAT'd players share one bucket and address rotation remains a deterrent rather than an absolute cap. The public card catalogue shares one budget with the token-bearing reads. The sliding-window algorithm now exists in three places — EOP-152 filed to migrate the join and creation limiters onto SlidingWindowCounter, deliberately not done here because ADR-019 makes the join throttle a primary security control.

Evidence

./mvnw clean verify BUILD SUCCESS — 1336 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; SpotBugs 0 findings; JaCoCo all coverage checks met with SlidingWindowCounter at 100% instruction and 100% branch (18/18); Javadoc and Checkstyle clean. npm run verify green in ui/ (typecheck, ESLint, Vitest, production build).

EOP-89.renderedBody:
Delivered — merged to main as 7d30fb2 (PR #115)

All five acceptance criteria met

AC-1 — both dependency trees scanned. A new dependency-cve job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs tools/supply-chain/scan-dependencies.sh, which scans pom.xml (Maven, transitively — CVE-2026-49844 was found at depth 3 via log4j-to-slf4j, proving real resolution rather than a shallow read) and ui/package-lock.json (npm — the lockfile, because every version in ui/package.json is a caret range). A separate CI job rather than ./mvnw verify, which this AC explicitly permits and which ci.yml twice insists on by requiring the build job stay Java-only and fast.

AC-2 — failure policy explicit, documented and demonstrated. Gates on HIGH and CRITICAL only, matching audit-plugins.sh's existing gating set. The divergence from build-quality.md's SpotBugs high/medium posture is argued rather than glossed: a SpotBugs medium is in our own code and always actionable, whereas a third-party transitive medium is frequently unreachable, often has no in-range fix, and arrives at a volume set by other people's release cadence.

Demonstrated in six steps by reintroducing the real HIGH this ticket fixed, so the demonstration doubles as proof the version override is load-bearing:

Step Condition Result
1 branch as merged, empty allowlist exit 0
2 postgresql.version reverted to 42.7.11 exit 1 — HIGH CVE-2026-54291 with no entry
3 allowlist entry expiring 2027-02-22 added exit 0, suppression printed
4 same entry, expires set to 2026-08-01 exit 1 — "re-argued, not re-dated"
5 fix restored, entry left in place exit 1 — "DELETE the entry"
6 entry deleted exit 0

AC-3 — suppressions reviewed, with a reason and an expiry. tools/supply-chain/accepted-cves.json, modelled on accepted-advisories.json but with two deliberate divergences. Eleven mandatory fields including a prose reachability trace and the `expires` field the existing model lacks. Keyed ID@module rather than by bare ID, because CVE-2026-59889 was measured hitting com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind in the same scan — a bare key would have suppressed both when only one was traced. The file ships empty, which is the correct steady state.

AC-4 — ADR. ADR-050, amended in place and dated after the incident below.

AC-5 — runtime measured. 4.75 s warm for both scan passes, plus 3 s for the Maven resolve step; ~6 s more on a cold Trivy DB (108.82 MiB). Two caches keyed differently on purpose: /.cache/trivy by UTC date, ~/.m2/repository by POM hash. Observed in CI at 17 s warm.

Six real vulnerabilities found and fixed, not just a scanner installed

The scanner found 1 HIGH and 5 MEDIUM on main. All six were closed by four patch-level overrides of Spring-Boot-parent-managed properties — postgresql 42.7.11→42.7.12 (CVE-2026-54291, MITM protection bypass via SCRAM-SHA-256, the only HIGH and the only directly-declared dependency), jackson-2-bom 2.21.4→2.21.5, jackson-bom 3.1.4→3.1.5, log4j2 2.25.4→2.25.5.

So the gate arrived green rather than red. A gate that is red the day it lands gets switched off rather than fixed.

The gate's exit contract earned its keep on day one

The job's first CI run failed — 429 Too Many Requests from Maven Central, Retry-After: 1800, on spring-data-bom. The script exited 2, not 0, refusing to report a clean tree from a scan that could not resolve the tree.

The root cause was a claim this change made about its own design: Trivy resolves the Maven tree with its own parser rather than invoking Maven, so the job originally carried no setup-java. True of the parser, false of the job — the parser keeps no cache and re-fetches every parent POM on every run, enough to trip Central's limiter from a shared CI address. Fixed with setup-java, an ~/.m2/repository cache sharing the build job's restore prefix, and a ./mvnw B dependency:resolve step. `-offline-scan` was refused: it would silently shrink the tree Trivy believes exists, an under-report presented as a clean scan — the one failure mode this design refuses.

The false claim had shipped in four documents. All four were corrected, and ADR-050's amendment is dated and states explicitly what is not amended, so the audit trail survives.

Sign-off

All five DoD gates returned VERDICT: APPROVE against the merged commit 3b3cb59 — @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian, @tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api. Two findings they raised (an undated ADR amendment; -q suppressing the very output that diagnosed the incident) were remediated rather than deferred, and all five were then re-dispatched rather than carrying earlier approvals forward. ./mvnw verify green throughout: 1280 tests, 0 failures, all coverage checks met. All five CI jobs green.

Follow-ups filed

EOP-146 (unguarded heredoc vs the exit contract), EOP-147 (gating logic has no automated test), EOP-148 (nothing detects an override overtaken by the Boot parent), EOP-149 (promote to a required check), EOP-150 (no complete-field-set API test), EOP-151 (stale plugin count in ci.yml).

Costs accepted, not hidden

The four overrides are rot liabilities with no automated check (EOP-148). The scan reads the resolved tree, so ADR-047's H2 exclusion is not honoured and an H2 CVE would gate falsely — the safe direction of that error, but real. EOP-92.renderedBody:
PR open and all CI checks green: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/86 (build, ui, image all pass). Branch eop-92-deal-every-card, 4 commits. Awaiting human review and merge.

Acceptance criteria — evidence

1. Every card is dealt; nothing is discarded. Hands.deal() loses the handSize/keptSize truncation, the mutable workingDeck copy and the whole Tampering scan-and-swap block. The loop runs to orderedDeck.size().

2. Correct seat-order distribution. 3 players 23/23/22, 4 players 17/17/17/17, 5 players 14/14/14/13/13, 6 players 12/12/11/11/11/11 — all summing to 68 with nothing discarded. Independently re-derived by @tester-unit-and-quality and confirmed against HandsTest, the ADR-023 amendment and openapi.yml.

3. The opening-lead card can no longer be discarded. It is now total by construction rather than by a swap: the lowest Tampering card is in the deck, so it is in a hand. NoTamperingCardDealtException is deliberately kept and remains reachable for a deck containing no Tampering card at all — @security-auditor confirmed it still fails closed, throwing before any deal is persisted or any event published.

4. Regression coverage, mutation-verified. Restoring the truncation fails 10 HandsTest tests, with the new shouldDiscardNothingAtAnyTableSize conservation guard failing at 3, 5 and 6 players but not at 4 — because 68 ÷ 4 = 17 exactly, so four players lose nothing under truncation either. The guard discriminates rather than blanket-failing. Also added: shouldPlaceTheSurplusOnTheLowestSeats, shouldDealTheFinalCardOfTheDeck, and TrickTest.shouldCompleteAShortFinalTrick (whose third assertion, that the same trick reads incomplete when the exhausted seat is wrongly said to hold a card, is what makes it discriminating rather than tautological).

5. Build green. ./mvnw verify — 1226 tests, 0 failures, SpotBugs BugInstance size is 0, All coverage checks have been met., 0 checkstyle violations. Hands itself is at 99.1% instruction and 95.0% branch coverage; removing the branch-heavy swap improved it.

6. End-to-end against a rebuilt local stack. Three real players over https://localhost/api/v1 after ./scripts/update-local.sh: dealt 23/23/22, TOTAL DEALT = 68, zero duplicate cardIds, 68 plays (up from 66 — the 68th is the short final trick resolving with seat 2 empty), status COMPLETED, leaderboard 200.

A defect found that was not in the request

EOP-72's mitigation swapped the lowest Tampering card to index keptSize - 1. Since keptSize = floor(D / n) x n is a multiple of n by construction, (keptSize - 1) mod n is identically n - 1 — so the swap could only ever land on the last seat. Whenever it fired (~2.9% of three- and six-player games, ~4.4% of five-player, never at four) the opening lead was handed deterministically to the highest-seated player. It was invisible to a green build because every test asserted hand sizes, and a swap to a fixed index satisfies those by construction. This is the stronger justification for the revert and is recorded in the ADR-023 amendment.

Recorded honestly alongside it: removing the swap makes the lead shuffle-determined, not uniform — each seat's probability is proportional to its hand size (0.338/0.338/0.324 at three players), exactly uniform only at four. @security-auditor raised that over-claim before any document made it, and ADR-023 now forbids restating it as uniformity.

Five DoD gates — all approved, two after rejection

  • @tester-unit-and-quality — REJECT, then APPROVE. Rejected on two stale comments in TrickControllerIntegrationTest still describing the discarded-remainder rule, one sitting directly above the loop whose hand.isEmpty() guard exists precisely because seats do not all run out together. Remediated by fixing both and then sweeping the repository for the same defect class, which found three more.
  • @tester-api — APPROVE. Confirmed EOP-83 divergence 1 fully resolved and every asserted status code and JSON path verified against controller and GlobalExceptionHandler source.
  • @security-auditor — APPROVE. Verified the shuffle is unbiased Fisher-Yates over a self-seeded SecureRandom with no settable seed, that Hand/Hands remain deeply immutable so dropping the defensive copy is safe, and that no DTO exposes another player's card count or contents. Net assessment: a security improvement.
  • @code-reviewer — APPROVE. All four gates green including tsc --noEmit, eslint and 168 front-end tests.
  • @architecture-guardian — REJECT, then APPROVE. See below.

The architecture rejection, and why it mattered

Two Documentation Gate defects, both introduced by me, neither a code defect:

1. The ADR-023 index row had ~6.4 KB of its own prose pasted past the terminating pipe, giving a four-column table a five-cell row. GFM discards cells beyond the header count, so that text vanished from the rendered index while sitting in the source — and the row that vanished was the one this story exists to correct. Fixed, and then fixed at the level of the mechanism: AdrIndexConsistencyTest gains a fifth invariant, shouldGiveEveryRowTheDeclaredColumnCount, which counts cells the way a renderer counts them. The reviewer verified by mutation that it fires on a deficit cell as well as a surplus one, and that it survives a legitimate table widening without needing an edit — a tripwire on the world, not a snapshot of a value.

2. ADR-042 still asserted the runtime deals 66 cards, which would have left two ADRs disagreeing about the current code. It now carries a dated part-supersession recording that divergence 1 closed in favour of the spec.

EOP-83

Divergence 1 (deal card count) is resolved by this story — in favour of the spec, since openapi.yml had documented the full deal correctly all along and the implementation was what drifted. Only divergence 2 remains open: the leaderboard is documented as available in any session state but returns an undocumented 409 unless the session is COMPLETED.

Deferred with tickets, all linked Relates

  • EOP-93 — sweep the ~11 surviving 74-card references left by EOP-75, in src/ as well as docs/. Trick.java:489-492's worked example is now unreachable and should go first.
  • EOP-94 — no test asserts the opening leader is not a fixed seat.
  • EOP-95 — nothing detects code drifting from the hand-authored OpenAPI contract; three documents were simultaneously stale during the EOP-72 period with a green build.

EOP-95.renderedBody:
Resolved by PR #120 on branch eop-95-openapi-contract-drift-gate, recorded as ADR-054.

Option (b) adopted as a JUnit build gate. OpenApiContractDriftTest fetches the springdoc-generated document from /v3/api-docs and compares it against docs/api/openapi.yml bidirectionally on two axes — path+method bijection and declared response status codes per operation. Reading the generated document means the gate cannot disagree with what Spring actually serves. No allow-list: the whole surface is covered, so GET /health is now authored into the contract rather than excluded.

Options (a) and (c) rejected with reasoning in the ADR. (a) fires on pure refactors and is trivially satisfied by a whitespace edit to the YAML, so it trains a token edit rather than a correct one. (c) is exactly the "resolved by a promise" outcome criterion 3 forbids as the sole remedy — three documents were missed on this very story while checklists existed.

Acceptance criteria

  1. ✅ ADR-054 carries a first-class "What the mechanism does NOT catch" section, stating outright that the gate would not have caught EOP-72, plus schema/property drift, reachability, proxy-layer contributions beyond one declared 413, and parameters/headers/security/tags.
  2. ✅ Four deliberate-drift experiments with verbatim failure output in the PR body. Notably experiment C — a dishonest PROXY_PRODUCED entry — produces two failures rather than none, so the declared-exception list is a required claim, not an escape hatch.
  3. n/a — a mechanical check was adopted.

What the gate forced. Making the annotated surface truthful was the bulk of the work and exposed a standing api-design rule violation: SessionController had @Operation on all five methods and @ApiResponse on none (springdoc reported a bare 200 each, including POST /api/v1/sessions which returns 201), and every GET across four controllers was missing ADR-051's 429. Each added status was traced to its emitter rather than added to go green.

Build: serial ./mvnw clean verify → Tests run: 1351, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, SpotBugs 0, JaCoCo all checks met (97.0% instructions, 88.9% branches).

DoD: all five gates returned VERDICT: APPROVE — @tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian. One finding acted on: a stale count in the guard's own Javadoc, whose investigation surfaced a worse error both reviewers had missed (the sentence named the wrong test — the two comparison directions are not interchangeable).

Where a figure was load-bearing it was kept with its derivation stated; where it was incidental historical colour it was dropped, exercising criterion 1's "no figure" branch.

Guard question: yes, worth adding — invariant 3

DeckArithmeticClaimsTest gained a third invariant deriving both figures from CURRENT_DECK_SIZE. It is sentence-scoped, strips Jira keys, and fires only where a sentence prices a read.

The review caught this story committing its own defect

@architecture-guardian rejected the first version and proved it by simulating the next deck trim against the shipped predicate: 1 of 4 sites caught. Two causes. spell() had no word for 70, and an unspellable number fails to match silently — so the guard would have gone quiet while reporting success, with the changelog and the test's own javadoc both promising it was trim-proof. And line scoping was invalidated by this very fix's rewrap, which left "= seventy" ending one line and "round trips" beginning the next — the primary site moved out of reach, and sentencesOf's own javadoc had already argued that "a line-scoped matcher would miss exactly the paragraph-length claims that go stale".

The migration <comment> was corrected in place. ChangeSet.generateCheckSum() in liquibase-core 5.0.3 digests only getChanges() and getSqlVisitors(), never getComments() — verified by decompilation and independently reproduced by @security-auditor. The green build deliberately does not corroborate this: every test context reads the same new file into a fresh schema, so a comment-inclusive checksum would recompute identically and pass. An earlier draft of the changelog claimed that replay as empirical confirmation; that overstatement was retracted in 221a2d5.
