Nominated as the canonical ticket for the missing `docs/architecture/building-blocks.md`. EOP-47 and EOP-116 are now linked to this one as duplicates.

Found during the EOP-41/EOP-49 gate round (PR #105). @architecture-guardian raised the missing arc42 static view as a finding, and a search before filing a new ticket turned up three open tickets for the identical gap, none referencing another:

  • EOP-47 (2026-08-12, from the EOP-14 Slice A review)
  • EOP-97 (2026-08-18, raised by @architecture-guardian while approving EOP-93/PR #87) — this one
  • EOP-116 (2026-08-20, from the EOP-58 gate round)

Its own verdict on that: "Three tickets for one gap is the backlog equivalent of the drift this PR exists to fix." Filing a fourth would have made it worse, so nothing new was created; EOP-47 and EOP-116 should be closed as duplicates of this ticket once someone with authority to close them agrees.

One correction to this ticket's scope, established by command rather than assumption. ls docs/architecture/ returns exactly two files, C4-Diagrams.md and runtime-view.md. So this is not an "audit the file" or "author the file" task with a settled answer — the file does not exist, while AGENTS.md and the @architecture-guardian operating protocol both name it as though it does. An agent instructed to read a file that is not there is the actual defect, and it has two defensible remedies:

  1. Create the document, or
  2. Remove every reference to it and record in an ADR that C4 Level 3 is deliberately the only static view.

If creating it, resist duplicating `C4-Diagrams.md`. A building-blocks view that restates the container diagram in prose becomes a second place to drift — precisely the failure EOP-41 and EOP-49 spent a story correcting, and the same file is already carrying that load: because C4 Level 3 has absorbed the static-view role, C4-Diagrams.md has grown past a thousand lines and now contradicts itself about the trick-play surface (:81-84 versus :1081-1089), filed separately as EOP-128. Prefer moving content out of C4-Diagrams.md over copying it, leaving a pointer at the origin.

Acceptance criteria (superseding whichever of the three tickets' criteria conflict)

  • Either docs/architecture/building-blocks.md exists with content not duplicated from C4-Diagrams.md, or every reference to it is removed and an ADR records C4 Level 3 as the static view.
  • EOP-47 and EOP-116 are closed as duplicates of this ticket.
  • If content moves out of C4-Diagrams.md, the origin keeps a pointer rather than a copy.
  • Any line citation in new content is re-derived from source, never adjusted by an offset.
  • ./mvnw verify green — the prose gates walk all of docs/*/.md, so a new file there is inside their reach.
  • docs/adr/README.md updated if an ADR is added or amended.

EOP-105.renderedBody:
Fixed on eop-105-ui-enum-drift, PR https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/92 (commit b4f64cc).

All six acceptance criteria answered

AC-1 met. PLAYER_ROLES = ['FACILITATOR', 'PARTICIPANT'] and SESSION_STATUSES = ['LOBBY', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'COMPLETED', 'ABANDONED'], as as const arrays with derived unions rather than inline unions — keeping the members at runtime is what makes them checkable.

AC-2 reported as not met on its premise, rather than ticked. The AC asserted the dead branching lives in ui/src/components/. It does not, and never did. There is no role === 'PLAYER' and no status === 'ENDED' anywhere in ui/src. Every production role comparison tests 'FACILITATOR', which was valid on both sides of the drift. All 'PLAYER' occurrences were test fixtures, now corrected. Three review gates confirmed this independently. The ticket's "any role === 'PLAYER' branch is dead code" describes a branch that never existed — worth annotating so the claim does not outlive the story.

AC-3 met, and the ticket's premise on `ABANDONED` was weaker than filed. COMPLETED was a genuine dead end and now exits the lobby via onSessionEnd(). ABANDONED deliberately gets no branch: SweepExpiredSessionsUseCase → abandonAndDelete sets the status and deletes the row in the same transaction, so no client can observe it — the next fetch is a 404, already handled. It is listed for contract fidelity only. Separately, SessionStatus's javadoc claimed "No code reaches this state yet", which was false; it now scopes the unobservability to the one path that writes it today and admits a second writer would make it observable with no test failing.

AC-4 met — ConnectionStatus tightened to 'CONNECTED' | 'DISCONNECTED', and LeaderboardDto.sessionStatus tightened from bare string in the same pass.

AC-5 met — Vitest asserts every declared member accepted and non-members rejected, including the two that had drifted.

AC-6 met: codegen rejected, with the reasoning and its limits recorded. ADR-009 carries a three-option decision table; the mirror is small and a generator would be a stack decision needing its own ADR. Enforcement is instead EnumMirrorParityTest, a new Java documentation-integrity test comparing the Java enums, the enum: lists in docs/api/openapi.yml and the as const arrays in ui/src/api.ts — four mirrors × two directions = 8 cases. It is Java rather than Vitest because ui/ deliberately has no @types/node, so a browser test cannot read files off disk.

Two things found that were not in the ticket

`StrideCategory` was a fourth mirror in the same condition — a bare union whose own comment asserted parity while nothing checked it, with SUIT_LABELS keyed exhaustively off it, so a drifted member would have taken the label map with it while tsc stayed green. It had not yet drifted, which is exactly why it was worth pinning. Found by a review agent during this story's own gate round, not by the build — the registration hole documented as a possibility fired within one review cycle.

Two known limitations, stated plainly: nothing detects a fifth unregistered mirror, and the guard reads only the export const NAME = [...] as const; idiom, so registering a bare-union mirror means rewriting the declaration first.

Verification

npm run verify in ui/ → exit 0, 178 tests. ./mvnw verify → exit 0, 1244 tests, SpotBugs 0, JaCoCo 96.9% instruction / 88.6% branch against 80/70.

Mutation-tested rather than merely green. Reintroducing ['FACILITATOR', 'PLAYER'] failed exactly one of the eight parity cases with a diagnostic naming the file — so the guard discriminates rather than failing broadly. @tester-unit-and-quality then ran five further mutations independently; none survived.

Definition of Done

All five gates approved. It took four rounds: @architecture-guardian rejected three times, and each rejection found something real — twice including prose that asserted a rule the code contradicted, which is the defect class this story exists to close.

@security-auditor answered the obvious question directly: enum drift on a role field in a game called Elevation of Privilege is not a privilege escalation, on two independent grounds — the client branch was never wrong, and the server recomputes the role from the opaque token before applying canStartPlay().

Follow-ups filed

  • EOP-108 — the boundary asserts rather than parses, and the new guards have no production callers. The root cause, deferred deliberately because it needs an error-contract decision first.
  • EOP-109 — three DTO fields still bare string where the contract declares an enum.
  • EOP-110 — six CVEs in the ui/ dev toolchain, one critical; production tree reports 0.

EOP-106.renderedBody:
Decision: the port moves back to 5173

The ticket asked whether 5371 is deliberate or a transposition. Git history answers the first half, and the author answered the second.

The premise in ADR-009 was wrong — but so was the port

ADR-009's ### Why the front-end port is :5371 says the value is "very likely a typo in the original commit". git log – ui/vite.config.ts shows that is false on both halves:

Commit Subject Port
7efd900 EOP-9 Done feat: serve a React front end behind Caddy on one origin created the file with `5173` — Vite's default, correct
496d7b5 EOP-63 To Do chore: set Vite dev server port to 5371 2026-08-17, +1/-1, sole change `5173` → `5371`
aab329f EOP-110 Done chore: clear six CVEs… touched only the import line

So the original commit was correct, and a later dedicated commit — whose subject line names the new value — introduced 5371. That sentence in ADR-009 has to be corrected whichever way the port goes.

Author's answer closes it

Asked whether the 2026-08-17 change dodged a port clash: "I got the port number wrong. I had no reason for changing the port number."

That is the one thing no amount of repository archaeology could establish, and it removes the only argument for keeping 5371. A non-default port with no reason behind it is pure carrying cost: every doc site has to explain the deviation, and the explanation is "someone mistyped it". Reverting to 5173 deletes the exception instead of documenting it.

Note this is the opposite of inventing a rationale. @architecture-guardian's objection on EOP-40 was to an ADR asserting intent behind a probable typo; recording an author-confirmed mistake is the honest alternative, and it means ADR-009 no longer needs a ### Why the port is … section at all.

Scope

  • ui/vite.config.ts — server.port → 5173
  • Four documentation sites updated in the same commit (AC#2): AGENTS.md, docs/devops/local-development.md, and two live claims in ADR-009
  • ADR-009's ### Why the front-end port is :5371 is superseded by a dated amendment, not deleted (AC#2)
  • ADR-009's original Development-workflow line stays untouched — preserved historical text, per the ticket

AC#4 and AC#5 already verified

A repo-wide search for 5371 finds it in no operational file. Confirmed absent from ui/Caddyfile, ui/Dockerfile, compose.app.yml, docker-compose.yml, .env, .env.example, .envrc, scripts/, .githooks/ and .github/. There is no .vscode/ or .idea/ directory in the repository. Nothing operational changes — only vite.config.ts and prose. CHANGELOG.md's two mentions stay as-is: they are records of past changes, not live references.

Follow-up filed separately

496d7b5 is prefixed EOP-63 To Do , but EOP-63 is "Add EoP card images to docs/EoP_Microsoft_Docs/cards/". That violates .opencode/rules/git-commits.md and is the direct cause of this ticket existing: with no port ticket to record against, the rationale (that there wasn't one) was never captured. Raised as its own issue.

EOP-107.renderedBody:
Delivered on branch eop-107-frontend-security-hardening — PR https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/97 (2 commits, 8 files, +387/−6).

Item 1 — cross-origin isolation headers: FIXED. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp added to both the site header block and the handle_errors block in ui/Caddyfile, so the success path and the error path stay header-for-header identical. require-corp is safe because there is no cross-origin subresource: the only external URL in the front end is the footer Creative Commons link, which is a navigation, and the GOV.UK CSS and fonts are copied into the bundle and served from /assets. Verified in the built artefact and on the wire. Trusted Types declined (needs a policy in application code and its failure mode is visible only in a real browser, which nothing in the pipeline runs) and nonce-based CSP declined (a static file_server cannot rewrite index.html per request, and Vite emits only external content-hashed files so default-src 'self' already refuses inline script). Both declines are recorded in ADR-035 with revisit triggers.

Item 2 — IP-literal header bypass: FIXED for every address a local browser can use; residual recorded. Site address widened to localhost:8080, 127.0.0.1:8080, [::1]:8080. https://127.0.0.1/ previously returned an empty 200 with Server: Caddy and none of the headers; it now returns 200 with all eight, as does https://[::1]/. An arbitrary unmatched Host still gets the bare empty 200 — recorded in ADR-035 as not closed, with the two ways out (a real certificate, or on-demand TLS behind an ask endpoint) named and rejected as disproportionate for a loopback-only demo. Worth noting for the record: what closed this was HTTP Host routing, not certificate issuance. Caddy did mint 127.0.0.1 and [::1] leaves, but RFC 6066 forbids an IP literal in SNI, so the localhost leaf is still the one presented and the browser name-mismatch warning is unchanged.

Item 3 — production source maps: FIXED in two layers. build.sourcemap: false in ui/vite.config.ts, so nothing is emitted (find /srv -name '*.map' in the built image returns nothing); plus @sourcemap path *.map → error 404 at the edge, because the SPA try_files fallback would otherwise answer a .map request with index.html and a 200, hiding a regression instead of reporting it. error rather than respond so handle_errors re-applies the headers and the 404 is byte-identical to any other.

Item 4 — `playerToken` in `sessionStorage`: re-examined and UPHELD, with the exposure now stated in ADR-015. The finding is correct and is not disputed: a script executing in this origin reads eop_session and holds a player's full authority for the life of the tab, which an HttpOnly cookie would take off the table. It stands because per-tab scope is the mechanism the demo actually uses for several seats in one browser, because the custom header is what keeps CSRF out of the threat model entirely, and because the SSE transport is built on fetch precisely so it can set that header — so moving to a cookie is a transport change, not a storage change. The amendment states plainly that the listed mitigations narrow the routes and do not prevent exfiltration by a script that already runs, and names three revisit triggers.

Items 5 and 6 — `.opencode/agents/ui-builder.md`: FIXED. New ### 5. Security section covering token handling (never localStorage, never in a URL or a log line, and exactly two modules touch it — App.tsx reads it out of storage behind its isStoredSession guard, api.ts attaches it to a request), never dangerouslySetInnerHTML, the CSP quoted in full with its practical consequences, the form-action 'none' convention (onSubmit + preventDefault(), never action, with the npm run dev false-negative spelled out), and an explicit prohibition on relaxing a CSP directive in ui/Caddyfile to make a component work.

Acceptance criteria. (1) Items 1–3 were judged independently and each is fixed. (2) Item 4's decision is recorded in ADR-015 in terms of the exposure accepted. (3) Items 5+6 closed together. (4) The CSP is byte-identical to main — diff on the directive returns nothing — so criterion 4's condition never fired; ADR-017 was amended anyway, because three new headers and a new refusal in the handler it describes would otherwise leave it silently incomplete. (5) Every header claim was measured against a running stack whose config was confirmed byte-identical to the committed file by md5sum inside the container, not read off the config.

Also amended: ADR-035 (three header-table rows, three dated narrowing pointers to prose the change falsified, and a new Amendments section), ADR-017, ADR-015, docs/adr/README.md (the ADR-035 index row said "five security response headers"; it now says eight), and CHANGELOG.md.

Definition of Done: all five gates approved — @tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian. @architecture-guardian first rejected on documentation synchrony (a stale index row and prose still asserting the pre-change position) and re-approved against commit f551627 after six remediation edits. ./mvnw verify and npm run verify both exit 0.

EOP-108.renderedBody:
Delivered — PR 93(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/93) open for human approval. Branch eop-108-ui-parse-response-dtos, commit 8f8dcb6, off main @ 211ca12.

Acceptance criteria

AC Discharged by
1. Decide and record the mechanism New [ADR-045](docs/adr/ADR-045-frontend-response-validation.md) — hand-written per-DTO parsers inside ui/src/api.ts. A schema library (Zod/Valibot) was rejected because ui/ has exactly three production dependencies and EOP-110 already tracks six dev-toolchain CVEs, so adding production supply-chain surface for ~11 shapes is disproportionate; codegen was deferred to ADR-009 as a stack decision. A re-open trigger is stated: "shape count roughly doubles or nested/recursive shapes appear"
2. Define the error contract before writing code, and reflect it in .opencode/rules/error-handling.md ContractViolationError extends ApiError with status = 502, thrown from the parser. Decided in ADR-045 §3 with both alternatives recorded as rejected. error-handling.md gains a ## Client side — the browser's own boundary section
3. Adopt the existing is* guards rather than duplicating them, or delete them — not both Adopted. All four guards are consumed through a single requireEnum(source, key, path, guard, members) seam that takes the guard and its as const array, precisely so no member list is re-inlined (EnumMirrorParityTest only sees the arrays). No second validation mechanism exists — @architecture-guardian verified this four ways
4. A Vitest case per boundary asserting an out-of-contract enum is rejected Ten rejection cases via it.each over a boundaries table, plus ten happy-path cases and twenty-two focused cases
5. Re-evaluate ADR-009's codegen rejection Its third revisit trigger — "runtime validation of responses is adopted (a parse rather than an assertion)" — fired. ADR-009 amended with a dated section: rejection upheld but on explicitly narrower grounds, since its original "three-enum, roughly twenty-line surface" argument is spent (api.ts went 525 → 883 lines). One new trigger registered

What changed

All ten JSON-returning helpers now parse instead of asserting. Twelve module-private parse* functions plus eleven shared validation primitives. The parsers are deliberately un-exported: that turns "api.ts is the only place a response is parsed" from a convention into a compiler-enforced property, and stops a vi.spyOn(api, …) test being mistaken for evidence that the boundary works.

startNewGame, dealCards (204) and subscribeToSession correctly get no parser — the SSE stream is a doorbell whose data: frames carry no DTO, and the re-fetch it triggers is parsed.

Strictness is bounded on purpose, and the bound must be quoted whenever this change is described: object-ness, required-field presence and typeof, arrays actually arrays, enum membership — but no format validation, no UUID regex, no ISO-8601, no ranges. The DTOs are structurally and enumerably validated; "validated at the boundary" unqualified over-claims.

This is not a security improvement and must not be cited as one. All three grounds on which this ticket recorded the EOP-105 deferral as defensible still hold. It closes a maintenance hazard — four exported guards that read as protection while protecting nothing — and converts silent misbehaviour into a loud failure.

Three items of unplanned scope

  1. `CardDto.suit` narrowed from bare string to StrideCategory. This closes the first of EOP-109's three items — commented on that ticket separately.
  2. `problemMessage` hardened — it read the error body as ProblemDetail and would render [object Object] into the error summary for {"detail": {…}}. Now type-checks detail/title and degrades to statusText. Deliberately not a DTO parser and must never throw.
  3. `requireNumberRecord` does not delegate to `requireNumber` — deliberate duplication, because its map keys are server-chosen and therefore payload. @security-auditor demonstrated a key like <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> being reflected into a message that renders in a GOV.UK ErrorSummary (escaped by React, not exploitable, but contrary to the never-name-the-payload rule). It now reports only the field, and builds its result with Object.create(null).

Verification

cd ui && npm run verify   → exit 0 — 9 test files, 220 tests (was 178, so +42)
./mvnw verify             → exit 0 — 1244 tests, BUILD SUCCESS
                            JaCoCo 96.9% instruction / 88.6% branch (vs 80/70)

The three component test files that stub global fetch pass unchanged — itself the evidence their fixtures were already contract-complete, since an incomplete one would now throw. No component or component test was modified.

Definition of Done — all five gates approved

  • @tester-unit-and-quality — APPROVE. Confirmed all ten boundaries covered and the toEqual(validBody) happy-path assertion is a real constraint. Identified three surviving mutants in the exactOptionalPropertyTypes conditional-spread absent arms; closed by eight further cases asserting Object.hasOwn(...) === false.
  • @tester-api — APPROVE. Field-by-field agreement against docs/api/openapi.yml and every Java DTO. Critically: no required field can legitimately arrive `null` or absent, so the parsers reject no valid response — the regression direction that mattered most. Confirmed TrickDto.ledSuit is the only outstanding bare-string contract enum.
  • @security-auditor — APPROVE. Verified the not-a-security-improvement framing is stated plainly and over-claimed nowhere; fail-closed at all ten boundaries and improved at two (no bogus admission reaches sessionStorage; no lifecycle transition fires on a rejected payload); prototype pollution structurally impossible; no production dependency added; EOP-110 posture unchanged. Its MINORs are fixed in this PR.
  • @code-reviewer — APPROVE. All twelve parsers read every declared field, all nested path strings correct and indexed, zero any, no surviving DTO assertion. Endorsed the un-export decision.
  • @architecture-guardian — APPROVE on the second round. It rejected the first round on two MAJORs, both legitimate and both remediated rather than downgraded: (1) docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md claimed api.ts owns "every wire concern" and then listed four, omitting validation, and runtime-view.md's running enumeration of refreshSession exits was stale — fixed, including a new section distinguishing three `onSessionEnd()` triggers from four distinguishable outcomes, now enumerated in full because an unenumerated count is uncheckable; (2) ADR-009 falsely claimed only a generator could close the field-coverage hazard — it cannot, since this repo already runs four text-reading comparison gates and a fifth would close it without a dependency, so the claim is deleted from both sites and the option set restated as three wide.

Known limitation carried forward

Because a parser reconstructs rather than passing the payload through, a field added to a DTO interface but not to its parser is silently dropped and arrives undefined while still typechecking — strictly worse than the as cast it replaced. EnumMirrorParityTest compares enum member lists, not field sets, so nothing detects it and enforcement is review only. Pinned as documented behaviour by a drops a field the server sends but no parser reads test, and registered as the one trigger that should reopen ADR-009's codegen rejection with the presumption reversed. ADR-009 now specifies concretely the text-comparison build gate that would close it without a generator.

EOP-109.renderedBody:
Scope reduced by EOP-108 — this ticket is now one field, not three.

EOP-108 (PR #93) narrowed `CardDto.suit` from bare string to StrideCategory and gave it a runtime parse via requireEnum(..., isStrideCategory, STRIDE_CATEGORIES). That was not scope creep for its own sake: EOP-108 was replacing every response assertion with a parse, and parsing every enum around suit while leaving that one field asserted would have been incoherent when isStrideCategory already existed and was already being consumed two lines away.

What remains. @tester-api audited every enum-typed field in docs/api/openapi.yml against what ui/src/api.ts now reads, and reported that `TrickDto.ledSuit` is the only outstanding bare-`string` contract enum:

  • docs/api/openapi.yml declares it allOf: $ref: '#/components/schemas/StrideCategory', so it is the STRIDE enum on the wire.
  • ui/src/api.ts reads it with optionalString, and TrickDto.ledSuit is still typed string. There is an inline comment at the field naming this ticket.
  • It is genuinely optional server-side — TrickDto is @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) and ledSuit is null until the first card of a trick is played — so any narrowing must keep it optional and must go through optionalString's replacement rather than requireEnum, which has no optional variant today. That is the one design decision this ticket still carries.
  • Every other enum-typed contract field is already narrowed and parsed: CardDto.suit and Card.suit (isStrideCategory), PlayerDto.role (isPlayerRole), PlayerDto.connectionStatus (isConnectionStatus), SessionStateDto.status and LeaderboardDto.sessionStatus (isSessionStatus). CardDto.rank is type: string in the contract rather than an enum schema, so bare string is correct there and it is not part of this ticket.

Please re-check the third item before starting. This ticket was filed as "three DTO fields still bare string where the contract declares an enum". One is now closed and one is identified above; if the third was CardDto.rank, it is not a defect. Worth confirming against the ticket's original evidence rather than assuming the count.

Two things EOP-108 leaves in place for you. The mechanism is decided — [ADR-045|docs/adr/ADR-045-frontend-response-validation.md], hand-written per-DTO parsers, bounded to structure and enum membership — so no new ADR is needed for a field narrowing that follows it. And .opencode/rules/error-handling.md now requires that the four is* guards be consumed, never re-inlined, because EnumMirrorParityTest only holds the as const arrays in three-way agreement with the Java enums and the OpenAPI enum: lists; a hand-written member list inside a parser would be invisible to that gate. Narrowing ledSuit therefore means routing it through the existing isStrideCategory seam, plus one Vitest rejection case proving an out-of-contract ledSuit is rejected rather than admitted.

EOP-109.renderedBody:
Delivered — PR 94(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/94), all five Definition-of-Done gates approved. Awaiting human approval to merge.

Scope, as it actually turned out

The ticket was filed as three bare-string fields. EOP-108 closed CardDto.suit first, so this story delivered one field: TrickDto.ledSuit.

The third item in the original list — CardDto.rank — was not in scope, but not for the reason the scope-reducing comment on this ticket gave. That comment said the contract declares rank as type: string rather than $ref-ing Rank, and therefore that bare string was faithful to the contract. That was false, and this ticket's own instruction to "re-check the third item before starting rather than assuming the count" was the right warning: docs/api/openapi.yml L995-996 is rank: / $ref: '#/components/schemas/Rank', there is exactly one rank: field, and there is no separate CardDto schema — both TypeScript interfaces map onto the one Card schema. Card.rank/CardDto.rank typed string is drift. It is accepted, fail-safe, recorded drift, which is a different thing from fidelity, and the difference is now stated correctly in six places rather than mis-stated.

What shipped

TrickDto.ledSuit is now readonly ledSuit?: StrideCategory, parsed by a new module-private optionalEnum(source, key, path, guard, members) that delegates to requireEnum once a value is present.

A helper rather than an inline check, because the field is genuinely optional on the wire — TrickDto is @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) and ledSuit is null until the first card of a trick is played — and requireEnum has no optional variant. The guard is passed in rather than the member list re-inlined, per .opencode/rules/error-handling.md, so isStrideCategory and STRIDE_CATEGORIES stay the single seam and remain visible to EnumMirrorParityTest. Net effect: optionality now weakens presence, never membership.

Two Vitest cases, both stubbing global fetch rather than vi.spyOn, so they exercise the real parser: an out-of-contract ledSuit rejects with TrickDto.ledSuit: expected one of SPOOFING, …, and ledSuit: null is still admitted as absent (Object.hasOwn false). Both would have passed vacuously under optionalString.

The three acceptance criteria that were decisions, not code

  • AC-2 — `Rank` mirror: REJECTED, not deferred. The client never compares or orders a rank: the contract supplies rankValue: integer described "Numeric rank used for comparison", the trick arithmetic that consumes it runs server-side, and the card face renders from rankSymbol. card.rank reaches exactly one consumer, cardImagePath(suit, rank), which returns string | null and whose every call site null-checks — so drift degrades to a missing card image, the same fail-safe shape suit had before EOP-108. Registering the mirror would additionally require teaching EnumMirrorParityTest.openApiEnumValues to read a YAML flow sequence. Exit condition recorded: revisit if rank ever becomes something the front end orders.
  • AC-3 — no new `mirrors()` row was needed, so it is satisfied vacuously. Stated explicitly in the code, the ADR and the changelog, because "no row needed" and "row forgotten" are indistinguishable in a diff — which is exactly how StrideCategory went unregistered until a review agent caught it during EOP-105.
  • AC-4 — `capturedBySuit` tightening: DECLINED. requireNumberRecord deliberately never inspects keys, because keys are server-chosen and ADR-045 §2 forbids reflecting them into a violation message. A Readonly<Record<StrideCategory, number>> index type would therefore be an unenforced compile-time claim — the exact defect class EOP-108 existed to remove. It would also be actively harmful: Record<K, V> over a finite union asserts total presence, so GameOverScreen.tsx's ?? 0 guard would look redundant to a future cleanup.

AC-5 — the exclusion lists in EnumMirrorParityTest.mirrors() and ADR-009 now describe the position after this ticket. No new ADR: ADR-045 already decided the mechanism, and a field narrowing that follows an existing decision is not a new one.

Gate outcomes — five approvals, four rejections survived

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE (after 2 rejections)
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE (after 1 rejection)

Both @tester-api rejections were factual and both were accepted in full: first the false type: string claim above, then a seventh site where the same over-claim survived in different words ("the last bare-string contract enum", which ledSuit was not). @architecture-guardian then rejected a correction for stating a non-operative cause — it had said a test-file rank list was invisible to the gate because of an idiom regex, when the operative reason is that typeScriptArrayValues reads only ui/src/api.ts and never opens the file at all.

The surviving lesson, recorded in CHANGELOG.md: a claim of this shape has to be swept for by *meaning, not by matching the phrasing of the first instance found.* Three of the four rejections were the same defect recurring in new words.

Verification

EOP-110.renderedBody:
Done — delivered in PR #95, merged to main as 19f75bd (commit aab329f).

Acceptance criteria

AC Result
1. Bump vitest, vite, nanoid, transitive esbuild past the advisory ranges ✅ vite ^5.4.9 → ^7.3.6, vitest ^2.1.3 → ^3.2.7. nanoid and esbuild cleared transitively — see below
2. npm audit 0 critical / 0 high, residual moderates recorded ✅ 0 vulnerabilities of any severity. No residual to record
3. npm run verify green ✅ exit 0 — Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 223 passed (223), 0 skipped, 0 todo
4. ./mvnw verify green ✅ exit 0 — Tests run: 1244, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 across 95 classes. EnumMirrorParityTest 8/8
5. Lockfile committed; engines.node satisfiable; CI builds on 22 ✅ lockfile committed; floor raised to >=22.12; CI `ui` job passed on Node 22

All six advisories cleared

vitest 3.2.7 (CRITICAL), vite 7.3.6 (HIGH), nanoid 3.3.18 (HIGH), esbuild 0.28.2, @vitest/mocker 3.2.7, vite-node 3.2.4 — verified in the installed tree, not just package.json. @security-auditor added a negative control: the pre-change manifests audited against the same live database in the same minute return 6 vulnerabilities (3 moderate, 2 high, 1 critical). So 6-before / 0-after is a real delta, not an offline no-op.

Three were cleared transitively rather than by a direct pin — nanoid only via vite → postcss ^8.5.6 → nanoid@3.3.18, so a direct dependency would have been a fiction; esbuild as vite 7's own dependency. No overrides, no resolutions, no new install scripts, universal integrity hashes, single registry host.

AC 1's coupling warning was correct, and resolved without a plugin major

@vitejs/plugin-react's declared floor rose ^4.3.2 → ^4.7.0 even though the installed 4.7.0 did not move: ^4.3.2 peers only vite ^4.2 || ^5, so leaving it declared a combination the plugin forbids under vite 7. Major 4 was kept — 4.7.0 already peers vite 7. @vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.0 was rejected as out of scope (it drags in a rolldown + React-Compiler migration).

npm's own suggested majors were declined

npm suggested vitest 4.1.11 + vite 8.2.1. Declined: every advisory range sits strictly below the installed 7.3.6 / 3.2.7 pair, so the majors close nothing extra — they are an artefact of npm audit fix computing from the old declared ranges. The cost would have been a 91-site vi.spyOn(api, …) refactor across five helpers in GameScreen.test.tsx (the ticket's own estimate was understated by >2×). Bundling that into a CVE fix would make the security change un-reviewable as a security change.

⚠️ Recorded honestly in ADR-009: the vitest-4 breakage is upstream guidance, not reproduced here. The ADR instructs confirming it against a real vitest 4 run before sizing the refactor, and striking the constraint if the pattern survives — so it cannot outlive its premise.

AC 4's warning about codemods

No file under ui/src/ was touched, so the as const enum mirrors were never at risk. Proven rather than assumed: git diff on ui/src/api.ts is empty and EnumMirrorParityTest passes 8/8.

Exposure was narrower than filed

npm audit -omit=dev was 0 before the change too, so nothing ever reached the shipped bundle. @security-auditor narrowed it further: the CRITICAL is unreachable in this repo at all (it needs a listening Vitest UI server; @vitest/ui is not installed and no script passes -ui), and two of the three vite advisories are Windows-only while the project runs darwin locally and ubuntu-latest in CI. What CI genuinely exposed was the install step, not the six advisories.

Scope additions

  • ADR-009 amended a fifth time (2026-08-20) with the docs/adr/README.md status row moved in step, as AdrIndexConsistencyTest requires. No new ADR — the constraint qualifies a choice ADR-009 already owns and is enforced mechanically by the ^3.2.7 caret. ADR-046 left unconsumed.
  • Five prose surfaces corrected. Four quoted the old versions/floor (AGENTS.md ×2, SETUP.md, docs/devops/local-development.md, ui/Dockerfile's stale dependency count). Separately, five places over-claimed that Node 22.0–22.11 fails npm install with EBADENGINE — with engine-strict unset and no .npmrc, npm warns and installs anyway. engine-strict=true was deliberately not added: it evaluates every package's engines, so it could hard-fail an install over an unrelated transitive declaration. That deserves its own ticket.
  • The EOP-40 CHANGELOG entry was deliberately not retro-edited.
  • Discharges a blocker on another decision: ADR-009's EOP-108 amendment rejected OpenAPI codegen partly because EOP-110 was open against this supply chain. A future codegen re-evaluation now inherits two live grounds, not four.

One new build warning, cosmetic and deliberately unsuppressed

esbuild 0.28 reports govuk-frontend's IE8–11 @media screen\0 hack in its minified CSS. Proved new (built main in a throwaway worktree: zero occurrences) and harmless (identical 140 selectors / 452 @media / 15 screen queries; sole delta @media ( → @media(, accounting for all 620 bytes of reduction). Not suppressed: the only lever silences the whole class and would hide a future CSS error that is genuinely ours.

Definition of Done — five of five

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE — proved vitest 2→3 dropped nothing by querying the installed module's collection globs (identical to v2) and running --reporter=verbose over all 223 cases
@tester-api APPROVE — scope claim verified by empty diffs on src/, docs/api/openapi.yml, ui/src/api.ts; full API integration suite enumerated green
@security-auditor APPROVE — the negative control, the lockfile supply-chain review and the per-advisory reachability analysis
@code-reviewer APPROVE — no blockers; confirmed the EBADENGINE mechanism, the 6 production packages and the vitest/config type augmentation from the installed package
@architecture-guardian APPROVE — reviewed its own stage-1 prose and found two MAJOR defects in it, both fixed

CI on PR #95: build, ui and image all pass — the image job additionally proves the container builds on node:22-alpine with the new toolchain.

Every figure above was re-run by me rather than inherited from a subagent. Two subagent claims were rejected: a fabricated "residual moderate esbuild false positive" (contradicted by its own 0-vulnerability output) and a NIT alleging the Node base image was bumped (the ui/Dockerfile edit is comment-only; FROM node:22-alpine is unchanged).

*Delivered. PR open for human approval: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/103*

Branch EOP-120-javadoc-enforcement, eight commits on main (a89760c).

All five Definition-of-Done gates approved

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE

It took six rounds, with four rejections. Every rejection was correct, and each is worth recording because they were all the same defect class this story exists to remove — prose asserting a mechanism the artefact does not contain:

  1. The false lookup claim survived at a fourth site — an XML comment directly above the addUniqueConstraint in 003-session-lifecycle.xml, in a stronger form than the original. My commit message had asserted a repo-wide grep confirmed no fourth site; it did not.
  2. I claimed debug=true fixed the Unable to compute stale date failure and cited a reproduction as verification. A five-attempt controlled experiment with the flag removed falsified it. Retracted at all four sites; the failure is now recorded as observed and unexplained.
  3. My "corrected" Maven plugin inventory named liquibase-maven-plugin as a peer plugin (it is not declared, though it is parent-managed at 5.0.3 without a lifecycle binding), and claimed maven-enforcer-plugin resolved from remote metadata (it was already parent-managed at 3.6.3 by spring-boot-dependencies). Both were guesses stated with the precision of measurements. Fixed by parsing the effective pom.
  4. The commit that fixed the prose garbled the prose — a search/replace applied twice, doubling clauses in .opencode/rules/build-quality.md, a file injected into every agent's context.

Acceptance criteria

Criterion Evidence
Build fails on missing Javadoc Checkstyle MissingJavadocType / MissingJavadocMethod at scope=public, minLineCount=-1, allowMissingPropertyJavadoc=false; JavadocMethod with both allowMissing*Tags=false. failOnViolation=true at the validate phase
Build fails on malformed Javadoc maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2, javadoc-no-fork at verify, failOnError, failOnWarnings, doclint=all,-missing. A deliberately broken {{ {@link}}} was injected and failed the build|
|IdentityTokenHash comment accurate|False paragraph replaced; verified against this JDK's MessageDigest source|
|MessageDigest.isEqual used|IdentityTokenHash.java:135, guarded by a source-text test so a silent revert to the generated equals fails|
|Full build green|./mvnw clean verify exit 0|

h2. Verification

./mvnw clean verify → exit 0. 1256 tests, 0 failures/errors/skips. 0 Checkstyle violations. javadoc:3.11.2:javadoc-no-fork on the cold path (No previous run data found, generating javadoc.). SpotBugs BugInstance size is 0. JaCoCo All coverage checks have been met, 141 classes. enforcer:3.6.3 with three rules passed.

h2. What the measurement actually showed

The useful finding is that there was almost no documentation debt. Tightening Checkstyle to full strictness surfaced exactly one violation across 157 files, plus four genuine public-API gaps and two hard doclint errors. The existing Javadoc was already complete with @param/@return tags — the lax settings had been hiding nearly nothing.

h2. Known limitations, recorded rather than smoothed over

* A comment-only edit to a `.java` file can now turn `./mvnw verify` red.
* A warm target/ may log Skipping javadoc generation…, and that is not proof the goal re-analysed your edit: the staleness record holds 117 paths, 92 jars, zero .java. CI is always cold, so merges are gated on full analysis; use clean verify locally after comment-only changes.
* One Unable to compute stale date failure remains observed and unexplained. clean is the workaround.
* Both Checkstyle Javadoc modules are scope=public, so an undocumented protected member on a public non-final class is uncaught. No live instance today; recorded in ADR-006 as a future amendment.
* maven-javadoc-plugin is not covered by tools/supply-chain/. The whole Maven layer is uncovered: fourteen bound entries against thirty-one managed, so bumping the Boot parent moves about thirty plugin versions in one line.

h2. Recorded durably

ADR-006 gains a 2026-08-20 (EOP-120) amendment for the sixth gate — and states plainly that its own "Plugins pinned to specific versions" line was inexact when written and remains inexact, since five of six declared plugins carry a version here. ADR-015 gains an amendment for constant-time comparison and the standing prohibition on keying a hash-based collection on IdentityTokenHash or Player. .opencode/rules/build-quality.md gains a sixth gate bullet; .opencode/rules/clean-architecture.md gains the {@code}not{{{@link}

}} rule for inner layers naming outer types.

Out of scope, with follow-up filed

src/test/java is not covered, and no package-info.java exists across the eight class-holding packages. EOP-121 is filed for those plus a MissingJavadocPackage module.

Item 1 of EOP-31 is closed by this work and noted on that ticket.

Closing evidence — all three parts delivered and merged

Status changed To Do → Done. The work was already delivered and merged before this transition; only the ticket had gone stale. Merged via PR #103, merge commit c1ef080, branch EOP-120-javadoc-enforcement.

See also the earlier comment of 2026-08-20 21:35, which records the five-gate DoD round in full. This comment adds independent re-verification of the merged result, plus two corrections to statements made in an earlier draft of it (below).

Part A — IdentityTokenHash corrected, comparison made constant-time

IdentityTokenHash.java:135 is now return MessageDigest.isEqual(asciiBytes(), candidate.asciiBytes());, replacing the short-circuiting String.equals a record would generate. The Javadoc now states that comparison happens in Java, in memory, and not as a database lookup (line 22), and points at Player#isIdentifiedBy (line 24). Locked against silent regression by IdentityTokenHashTest.java:168, which asserts the source text contains the MessageDigest.isEqual(...) call.

The real path the old comment misdescribed is GameSession.java:251 — players.stream().filter(player -> player.isIdentifiedBy(tokenHash)).findFirst().

Part B — javadoc gate added, with one deliberate deviation

maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2, bound to verify as execution verify-javadoc, goal javadoc-no-fork (plain javadoc forks a generate-sources lifecycle and re-runs earlier phases), with failOnError=true, failOnWarnings=true, show=public.

Deviation from the brief: the story asked for full doclint with all five groups including missing. Delivered config is doclint=all,-missing — a two-tool split in which Checkstyle owns missing and the javadoc plugin owns malformed (accessibility, html, reference, syntax).

Why, recorded in ADR-006 and CHANGELOG.md:

  • doclint's missing group ignores javadoc's -public flag and demands a comment on every private field — roughly 50 findings across the domain exception classes, none of them public API.
  • The apparent scoping fix doclint=all/protected is rejected outright: error: Access qualifiers not permitted for -Xdoclint arguments.

The missing half therefore landed in checkstyle.xml:74-95: new MissingJavadocType; MissingJavadocMethod with minLineCount 10 → -1 and allowMissingPropertyJavadoc → false; JavadocMethod with allowMissingParamTags and allowMissingReturnTag both → false; all at scope=public.

The tightening surfaced one Checkstyle violation, four genuine public-API gaps (ScoredPlay#components, two record-component @param tags on LeaderboardResult, one @param on TrickRepository#openTrick) and two hard doclint errors. The useful finding is that there was almost no documentation debt — the lax settings had been hiding nearly nothing.

Part C — build green on the cold path

./mvnw clean verify → exit 0. javadoc:3.11.2:javadoc-no-fork (verify-javadoc) ran with no "Skipping javadoc generation" line, so the gate genuinely analysed rather than hitting the documented warm-target/ false green. Tests run: 1256, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0. SpotBugs check and JaCoCo check-coverage both ran. BUILD SUCCESS.

AC1 / AC2 — proven empirically, not merely reasoned about

Verified by injecting deliberate violations into Main.java, then reverting:

  • Missing Javadoc and missing tags → ./mvnw checkstyle:check exit 1, with exactly three errors: MissingJavadocMethod: Missing a Javadoc comment., JavadocMethod: @return tag should be present and have description., JavadocMethod: Expected @param tag for 'undocumented'.
  • Malformed reference → an unresolvable {{ {@link}}} gave ./mvnw javadoc:javadoc-no-fork exit 1 with error: reference not found. This confirms the plugin half is load-bearing rather than decorative, which matters precisely because Checkstyle does all the missing work.

    After reverting, git status --porcelain is empty and both goals return exit 0.

    Note on AC wording: AC1 and AC2 are satisfied in outcome, but by a different mechanism than their text names. They attribute the build failure to a maven-javadoc-plugin doclint warning; it is in fact Checkstyle that fails the build. The required outcome holds; the attribution does not. Documented in ADR-006.

    h3. Two corrections to an earlier draft of this comment

    Both were claims stated more confidently than the evidence supported — the same defect class this story exists to remove, so they are corrected in place rather than quietly dropped:

    # I wrote that the false lookup claim existed at three sites. It was four. The fourth was an XML comment directly above the addUniqueConstraint in db/changelog/changes/003-session-lifecycle.xml, stating the claim in a stronger form than the original — which is why PR #103 touches that changelog at all.
    # I wrote that two gates initially rejected. The actual record is six rounds with four rejections, all four correct. One of them falsified a claim I had made that debug=true fixed the Unable to compute stale date failure; a five-attempt controlled experiment with the flag removed disproved it, and the failure now stands recorded as observed and unexplained, with clean as the workaround.

    h3. Documentation

    ADR-006 gains a 2026-08-20 (EOP-120) amendment for the sixth gate, and states plainly that its own "Plugins pinned to specific versions" line was inexact when written. ADR-015 gains an amendment for constant-time comparison and the standing prohibition on keying a hash-based collection on IdentityTokenHash or Player. .opencode/rules/build-quality.md gains a sixth gate bullet; .opencode/rules/clean-architecture.md gains the {@code}not{{{@link}

    }} rule for inner layers naming outer types. CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased].

Known limitations, recorded rather than smoothed over

  • A comment-only edit to a .java file can now turn ./mvnw verify red.
  • A warm target/ may log Skipping javadoc generation…, and that is not proof the goal re-analysed your edit: the staleness record holds 117 paths, 92 of them jars, and zero .java. CI is always cold, so merges are gated on full analysis; use clean verify locally after comment-only changes.
  • Both Checkstyle Javadoc modules are scope=public, so an undocumented protected member on a public non-final class is uncaught. No live instance today.
  • maven-javadoc-plugin is not covered by tools/supply-chain/, which audits the OpenCode npm plugins only. The whole Maven layer is uncovered.

Out of scope, with follow-up filed

src/test/java is not covered, and no package-info.java exists across the eight class-holding packages. EOP-121 is filed for those plus a MissingJavadocPackage module.

EOP-31 item 1 is closed by this work and noted on that ticket; its items 2–7 remain open, so EOP-31 stays in To Do.

EOP-122.renderedBody:
Resolved via option (b) — literal dropped, not homed. PR #104, three commits, all five DoD gates approved.

Disposition

Option (b) was chosen deliberately, as the ticket permits. AC 2 is therefore not applicable — docs/adr/ADR-006-build-quality-gates.md was not amended, its *Status:* line is untouched, docs/adr/README.md is untouched, and git diff main...HEAD – docs/ returns zero lines. @architecture-guardian ruled independently that option (a) would have been the wrong disposition and that it would have rejected it: an ADR records a decision this project made, and "the Boot parent happens to resolve liquibase to 5.0.3" is not a decision we took — no alternatives weighed, no consequence accepted — so it would have produced a decision record with no decision in it, while mis-signalling that the value is under our control.

The ticket's prohibition was honoured — no proposition was weakened. All four operative claims survive, and two gained precision:

Proposition Before After
liquibase is not one of the declared plugins ✓ ✓
liquibase-core executes during tests as an application dependency ✓ ✓
we declare no liquibase-maven-plugin ✓ ✓
the parent nonetheless manages one "it is parent-managed" "the Boot parent does carry one" — source named
nothing binds it, so it never runs "no lifecycle binding" "no <executions> and no <configuration>, so nothing binds it to a phase" — mechanism named
the version is 5.0.3 stated dropped, with the reason and the recovery command given

The new text also carries a standing instruction — "do not helpfully restore a literal" — at the exact site a future author would restore it, matching the prose-enforcement precedent database.md uses for the frozen NNN- sequence.

Grounds, ranked

@architecture-guardian required these be ranked rather than listed as equals, because one of them proves too much if cited alone:

  1. Guidance weight — decisive. Every operative proposition is true at any version, so the number was inert. A reader who knows 5.0.3 can do nothing they could not do without it.
  2. Not ours to pin — supporting only. It comes from the Boot parent's liquibase.version. But this cannot be the discriminator: the Boot-owned 3.12.0 on the same line is equally not ours to pin, yet correctly stays homed at ADR-006:100, because it is quoted contrastively to state we deliberately sit behind the parent at 3.11.2 — strip it and that proposition becomes unstatable. Guidance weight is the discriminator, not ownership. Anyone citing this precedent must lead with ground 1.
  3. Conflation risk. Of fifteen tracked 5.0.3 text sites, twelve concern liquibase-core — including ADR-006:59, the ADR's only mention, which states an unrelated contextFilter-precedence fact. Option (a) would have dropped a plugin assertion into the middle of that cluster, forty lines away.

AC 1 — met

grep -n '5\.0\.3' .opencode/rules/build-quality.md returns nothing.

AC 3 — met, with the full sweep

Site Literal Home
build-quality.md:6 3.11.2, 3.12.0, 3.6.3, 4.1.0 ADR-006:100/:102
build-quality.md:6 5.0.3 removed
build-quality.md:5 JDK ≥ 21 enforcer rule — mechanically enforced, not a pin
performance-testing.md:7 influxdb:1.8 docker-compose.yml:9 — now cited inline
versioning.md:1 SemVer 2.0.0 ADR-007:13/:37 — a spec version, immutable by definition
versioning.md:2 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT illustrative; corresponds to no real version, so nothing to diverge from

On the one judgement call: @architecture-guardian ruled decisively that docker-compose.yml:9 is an acceptable "dated supersedable home" — it is not a copy of the truth, it is the pin, executable, with version control supplying dating and commits supplying supersession. Demanding an ADR would create a second copy a compose bump silently falsifies, reinstating EOP-35's defect one file over. Reading AC 3 as "every literal needs an ADR" would absurdly force one for 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT.

performance-testing.md was also tightened: 1.8 appeared twice on main (lines 7 and 89), stated free-standing and attributed to nothing. It now appears once, at its citation.

AC 4 — met

./mvnw verify → Tests run: 1256, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS. Verified on the cold path too (./mvnw clean verify, full javadoc analysis). CI green on the exact SHA — run 32418426157, conclusion: success. All five documentation-integrity gates pass; none scans the three changed paths, and no test reads .opencode/rules/ at all (the single grep hit is a Javadoc mention at SessionLifecycleOffValueIntegrationTest.java:34).

DoD gate round — 5/5 approved

@tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian all returned VERDICT: APPROVE. Every one independently re-ran ./mvnw verify. Two gates rejected material and were remediated rather than argued with:

  • @code-reviewer challenged the entry's 31/14 effective-pom figures, reporting 34/17 with duplicates. I measured rather than conceding: direct <plugin> children are 31 and 14 with zero duplicates. Its 34/17 counted .//artifactId descendants, which pick up coordinates nested in <configuration>/<dependencies> blocks — hence the identical +3 offset in both sections and the phantom duplicates. It re-measured and withdrew both warnings. Corroborated four ways: my parse, @security-auditor's, @architecture-guardian's, and pom.xml's own EOP-120 figures.
  • @architecture-guardian found the CHANGELOG entry's own census was wrong — it said thirteen sites and claimed every one was liquibase-core, when the true figures are fifteen and twelve, with three plugin claims (pom.xml:164, CHANGELOG.md:59, CHANGELOG.md:20). Correct on all three sub-claims; fixed in commit three, which also records the trap that caused it: git grep emits Binary file … matches as a line, so three tracked PDFs under docs/EoP_Microsoft_Docs/ inflated the denominator while two CHANGELOG.md lines fell out of it. It also found the "doubled the stale-literal surface" claim false — see below — and both findings are now discharged.

Two findings deferred, both filed rather than dropped

  • EOP-126 — pom.xml:164 still carries a standing liquibase-maven-plugin 5.0.3 claim, same value, same parent property, same absence of any test. Found independently by @security-auditor and @architecture-guardian. It means this change's surface for the coordinate went from two sites to one, not zero to two averted, and the CHANGELOG entry was corrected to say so — shipping an overstating entry on a ticket about overstated claims would have been self-defeating. Deferred because it is outside AC 3's .opencode/rules/ scope, is co-located with the parent declaration that produces the value rather than sitting in a file injected into every agent's context every session, and does not contradict the new rule text; @architecture-guardian agreed, calling it un-tested rather than homeless.
  • EOP-127 — docker-compose.yml:9 homes InfluxDB's value, but ADR-016 records no rationale for the 1.x line, which matters because 2.x changed the write API and that write path is exactly what ADR-016 records as broken.

No new automated guard, with reasoning rather than omission

@architecture-guardian killed the obvious candidate explicitly: a RuleFileVersionLiteralHomeTest scanning .opencode/rules/.md for version-shaped strings and requiring each to appear in an authority file *would have PASSED F-1 — 5.0.3 was present at ADR-006:59 and eleven other authoritative sites. The defect was an unhomed proposition, and no digit matcher can distinguish liquibase-maven-plugin 5.0.3 from liquibase-core 5.0.3. A gate reporting "all literals homed" on the very tree containing this defect would be worse than no gate. The only structurally expressible neighbour — a dangling-ADR-citation check — would not have caught it either, since "ADR-006 as amended 2026-08-20" is a structurally valid citation. Enforcement stays with review plus the in-place inoculation.

State

PR #104 → main, three commits (fade9a2, 4273083, 4342a89), CI green, 5/5 gates approved. Awaiting human merge — not self-merged.

EOP-130.renderedBody:
Built, not closed won't-do. The cheaper alternative the ticket asked to be weighed first — an embedded re-derivable grep instead of a line number — is subsumed rather than rejected: the anchor is that grep, and it is machine-checked instead of relying on a reader to run it.

PR: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/121 (commit 12a33bc, branch eop-130-line-citation-gate)

Two corrections to the ticket's own figures

  • "Roughly thirty" citations was a five-fold undercount — there are 171 named citations across 21 documents.
  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ held seven gates, not five, so this is the eighth, not the sixth. The two the ticket omitted are JoinCodeSpaceClaimsTest (EOP-56) and OpenApiContractDriftTest (EOP-95).

What was built

src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/SourceCitationAnchorTest.java — 585 lines, 9 tests. Three checks:

Check Scope
Cited path resolves against a tracked file universal — all 171
Cited start and end lines exist universal — all 171
Explicit `{{ (anchor: }}token{{) }}` occurs inside the cited range opt-in — 21 today

Why anchoring is opt-in, and why the ticket's favoured option was wrong

The ticket preferred "assert the line is neither blank nor inside a javadoc comment", saying it "would have caught every EOP-49 defect". Measurement contradicts this: ~58 citations deliberately target javadoc, so a blanket comment rejection would produce dozens of false failures.

Automatic anchor inference was then prototyped and measured: it flagged 36 of 67 inferred anchors. The noise is irreducible, not a tuning problem — it cannot distinguish "cites the javadoc on purpose" from "drifted onto the javadoc", and drift-onto-javadoc was EOP-49's failure mode.

Opt-in bought a second, structural property the ticket did not anticipate: a citation quoted inside an immutable dated amendment block stays truthful as history. Two live cases depend on it — this ADR's own 2026-08-18 blockquote cites GlobalExceptionHandlerTest.java:553's new NoTamperingCardDealtException(78) when the live code is (68) at line 674, and ADR-006:44 states dated amendment blocks are immutable records; and ADR-027:77-78 carries a stale anchor that EOP-131 explicitly forbids editing in place. A semantically complete gate would have had to falsify history or grow an opt-out marker.

The tree was not clean on arrival — acceptance criterion 3's premise was false

The criterion assumed the citations "were all re-derived on 2026-08-21 under EOP-41/EOP-49". They were not; only those two tickets' own scope was. Seventeen live citations across six documents were drifted and are repaired.

The most serious was not a wrong number but a false architectural claim: ADR-023:1291 said Trick.reconstitute was the only caller of Trick.winningPlay(). reconstitute (line 147) takes a winner parameter and never calls it — the only caller is resolved() at Trick.java:438. Also: CARD_PLAYED's publish point was cited as PlayCardUseCase.java:229 (a closing brace) in three documents while a fourth already had the correct :253; and three application.yml flag citations pointed at a rate-limit key, a comment tail and a blank line.

The gate caught its own author twice

  1. The ADR amendment used invented placeholders File.java:123 to describe the syntax; shouldResolveEveryCitedPath failed on them within minutes of the gate landing.
  2. Sixteen anchors were written but only fourteen enforced, because two used a placement the pattern of the day rejected. A ninth test shouldParseEveryAnchorMarkerItFinds now fails the build on any anchor: marker the parser did not bind — an anchor that reads as enforced but is not is worse than no anchor.

A third instance came from the gate round: @code-reviewer found Dockerfile sat in the extension list but could never match, because the pattern demands a literal . before the extension. ui/Dockerfile:13 was silently ignored. Same hollow-coverage class; fixed with a dedicated alternation branch.

Acceptance criteria

  1. ✅ Gate exists under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/.
  2. ✅ Demonstrated failing on deliberate drift. Perturbing ADR-023:1290 from Trick.java:441 to :400 produced: docs/adr/ADR-023-…:1290 cites Trick.java:400 (anchor: winningPlay) — not found in the cited range; it occurs at lines 438, 441. Coverage limits are stated in the class Javadoc. Two floors carried: MINIMUM_CITATIONS = 150 (171 exist) and MINIMUM_ANCHORED_CITATIONS = 18 (21 exist) — both have been observed failing, so neither is vacuous.
  3. ⚠️ Satisfied, but the premise was false — see above. The two universal checks pass on the tree as it stands; the seventeen repairs were needed for the anchored subset.

Limits, stated plainly

  • ~122 bare `` `:N` `` continuation references are unchecked. They collide with port numbers (`{{ }}:8080{{ }}{{, }}{{ }}:5173{{ }}`) and their antecedent file is not mechanically recoverable — binding by "last named file" produced 17 spurious failures in the survey. Worth a follow-up to convert them to named form.

  • No proof of truth — the gate checks that a citation points where it claims, never that the claim is correct.
  • Two third-party ChangeSet.java references into liquibase-core are allow-listed.

EOP-132 warned this gate would be blinded by line-oriented scanning of long table rows. It is not: every regex match on every line is parsed, and docs/adr/README.md:23 alone contributes two anchored citations from one 1,271-word row.

EOP-136.renderedBody:
Scope addition raised during the EOP-31 five-gate review round, recorded here rather than by rewriting the description.

@architecture-guardian rated this MAJOR while reviewing EOP-31, and it is a distinct deliverable from adopting Testcontainers: the H2-versus-PostgreSQL-17 constraint-name residual has no durable home in the repository. It currently lives in exactly two places, a ## [Unreleased] bullet in CHANGELOG.md and this ticket. The changelog bullet becomes archaeology under a version heading at the next release, and this ticket disappears the moment it is closed — including if it is closed as won't-do. So the record gap can outlive every possible outcome of the work described above.

Two specific gaps were measured, not inferred:

First, docs/adr/ADR-024-trick-play-persistence.md is entirely silent on the subject. Grepping it for H2, Postgres, constraint name, substring and Testcontainers returns no output at all. The ADR that owns the trick-play persistence boundary says nothing about how that boundary translates constraint violations, nor on which engine that translation is verified.

Second, neither adapter's Javadoc mentions either engine. SessionRepositoryAdapter.java:217-234 and TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter.java:893-916 both carry good prose defending the choice to match on constraint name rather than exception type, and both state that an unrecognised name is rethrown so a new constraint fails loudly. That reasoning is sound, but it answers a different question. Nothing at either site says the names are matched against H2 message text while production runs PostgreSQL 17.

Added to the scope of this ticket, and each is worth doing independently of whether Testcontainers is ever adopted:

  • A Consequences entry in docs/adr/ADR-024-trick-play-persistence.md naming the engine gap explicitly.
  • One sentence at SessionRepositoryAdapter.java:217-234 recording that the two constraint names there are matched against H2 message text and are unverified on PostgreSQL.
  • The same at TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter.java:893-916 for its seven names.
  • If this ticket is ever closed without adopting a real engine in the test path, those three records must still be in place first. That is the condition that stops the residual becoming invisible.

EOP-145.renderedBody:
Delivered and merged to main via PR #114 (merge commit 3278055). CI green on all four jobs: build 1m53s, image 1m23s, ui 26s, supply-chain 29s.

Three commits: 341b2fd (feature), 86b67f9 (test remediation), be8045d (docs).

Two corrections to this ticket, both deliberate and recorded rather than quietly applied.

1. The feature flag as specified was not implementable. This ticket named eop.features.card-magnifier in application.yml, and Scenario 4 required that "the eop.features.card-magnifier bean is absent from the application context". Neither is possible, for two independent reasons: a CSS lens has no Spring bean for @ConditionalOnProperty to remove, and a Spring property is invisible to a bundle Caddy serves as static assets from a separate path (ADR-017). Per ADR-037, front-end flags are build-time Vite variables. The flag shipped is VITE_CARD_MAGNIFIER_ENABLED, wired through the seven touch points the VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED precedent establishes. Nothing was added under eop.features.*.

Scenario 4 is therefore SUPERSEDED, not dropped. It is satisfied instead by the ARG in ui/Dockerfile defaulting to false, and by the flag being tested in three positions rather than two — true, false, and unset — the last confirming that the === 'true' comparison is what makes an absent variable fail closed.

This is recorded in an ADR-037 amendment rather than fixed silently, because the ticket was written in good faith from the backend convention in feature-flags.md and the next front-end story would otherwise repeat it.

2. The magnifier magnifies pixels, not meaning. This was flagged during discovery and is worth restating on the ticket. A card's threatPrompt never reaches the visible DOM — it exists only in the card's aria-label — so a 2x scale enlarges card art and rank glyphs but does not surface threat text to a sighted player. If reading the scenario text is the real requirement, that needs a re-rendered text overlay, which is a different story and was explicitly out of scope here.

Scenario audit

  1. Lens on hand-card hover — MET
  2. Lens on trick-zone-card hover — MET (a new TrickCardFace component was extracted, because a hook cannot be called inside the .map that renders the plays)
  3. Tap to show, second tap or tap-outside to dismiss — MET
  4. No lens when the flag is off — MET as superseded, see correction 1 above
  5. Does not interfere with click or drag card play, dismisses on pointer-leave — MET. A mouse pointerdown hides the lens, because setPointerCapture would otherwise route every subsequent pointermove to the captured card and drag the lens across the table. A touch pointerdown pins it and still selects the card, because click-to-select plus "Play selected card" is the WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.7 single-pointer alternative to dragging and the magnifier must not consume it.
  6. Lens still appears on a disabled card — MET. A card you cannot yet play is precisely the one you most need to read.

Definition of Done — five of five approved

  • @tester-unit-and-quality — APPROVE, after one REJECT (see below)
  • @tester-api — APPROVE
  • @security-auditor — APPROVE, no findings
  • @code-reviewer — APPROVE, zero blockers
  • @architecture-guardian — APPROVE

The REJECT is the most useful thing in this ticket. @tester-unit-and-quality found the geometry tests were tautological: they imported LENS_ZOOM and LENS_DIAMETER_PX from the module under test and asserted against them, so mutating a constant moved the rendered value and the expectation together and the suite stayed green. The 2x was an explicit product decision, revised down from 3x during discovery, and the test meant to pin it could not. It also found the inner replica's offset — the - LENS_BORDER_PX correction that keeps the magnified pixel under the cursor — was never asserted at all, that the touch-pointermove guard was untested, and that the capture-phase document listener had no unmount test.

86b67f9 closes all of it, test-only, and each closure is proved by mutation: flipping LENS_ZOOM from 2 to 3 now fails two tests, dropping the border term fails one, removing the pointer-type guard fails one. Before the remediation all three mutations left the suite green.

Four limitations reviewed and accepted rather than fixed. Each is a trap for the next person in these files rather than a defect today, and all four are in CHANGELOG.md.

  • A flag-off build still ships the lens code. Building ui/ with the flag true, false and unset emits an identical 198,662-byte bundle with eop-card-lens present in all three. Vite substitutes the value and minifies but does not prune the component it guards, so the flag controls whether the lens renders, never whether it is compiled — an affordance control, not a security boundary. Now recorded in ADR-037 next to the analogous import.meta.glob paragraph.
  • The drag ghost duplicates CardBody and hardcodes 80/120/6 instead of the HAND_CARD_* constants, which is the exact drift CardBody was extracted to prevent. Left only because the ghost cannot itself be magnified.
  • The @media (max-width: 768px) rule shrinking .eop-card to 60x90 is dead, because CardFace sets the same properties inline and inline wins. It predates this story, but the lens geometry is now pinned to 80x120, so future responsive work must move the CSS rule and the lens constants together.
  • The 100px lens overflows the 80px card by 10px on each side with no overflow: hidden on the container, so a lens overlaps its neighbours in a dense hand. The current design accepts that in exchange for showing context around the magnified point.

Merge-dark deviation, disclosed. feature-flags.md says merge with the flag off. The ARG default in ui/Dockerfile is false, so a plain docker build ships dark, but .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/update-local.sh both pass =true so the deployed artefact carries the feature that was asked for. That is exactly the position VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED already occupies. Justified by the change being wholly presentational with no server surface, and by all five DoD gates running inside this story.

Build: npm run verify in ui/ — typecheck clean, lint clean, 240 tests in 10 files, production build green. ./mvnw clean verify — 1280 tests, 0 failures, SpotBugs 0, all coverage checks met. The five prose-integrity gates re-ran green after the docs edits (26 tests).

Pure front-end plus documentation. No Java, no endpoints, no migrations, no dependency changes — ui/package.json, ui/package-lock.json and pom.xml are byte-identical to main.

EOP-154.renderedBody:
Delivered on PR #123 — awaiting human approval to merge

Branch eop-154-repair-k6-influxdb-write-path, commits 392f898 (the repair) and d710ed4 (gate-review remediations).

The handed-down root cause was wrong, and there were three faults, not one

The diagnosis in this ticket — that the influxdb_data volume predated auth being enabled, so no admin user exists and every write 401s — does not reproduce. Probed against the live stack:

probe result
write with no credentials 401
write with the container's own $INFLUXDB_ADMIN_USER:$INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD 204
write with deliberately wrong credentials 401

Real credentials succeeding and wrong ones failing is a working auth setup. The timeline says why: auth was enabled on 2026-07-27 (cb9bd34), and the volume actually in use, eop-monitoring_influxdb_data, was created 2026-08-05 — after, so the seed credentials were honoured on its first init. (The older eop-threat-medeling_influxdb_data is the pre-name: orphan ADR-016 warns about; nothing mounts it.) The ticket's question "why are the configured admin credentials refused" is therefore void — they are not refused. That clause has been deleted from ADR-016 rather than carried forward.

The actual write-path fault is mundane: INFLUXDB_URL=http://localhost:8086/k6 carries no userinfo, so every k6 write was unauthenticated, and correctly 401'd.

Two further faults on the read path, recorded in no ticket, would each have left the dashboard empty on their own:

  1. The provisioned datasource took {{url: $ {INFLUXDB_URL}

    }} — a host address. access: proxy means Grafana makes the call itself, and inside that container localhost:8086 is Grafana. Proved from inside eop-grafana: curl localhost:8086/ping → connection refused (exit 7), curl influxdb:8086/ping → 204. One variable was serving two consumers with mutually incompatible requirements.

  2. The datasource declared no uid, so provisioning generated one (observed P951FEA4DE68E13C5) while all ten dashboard panels reference "uid": "InfluxDB". No panel could resolve its datasource.

Chosen option: B (auth disabled), per the PO's recommendation

INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED: "false", and INFLUXDB_ADMIN_USER/INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD deleted. Rationale, recorded in the ADR-016 amendment and accepted by @security-auditor: the port binds to 127.0.0.1 only, the database holds load-test timing samples with no application or personal data, and k6's only authentication route is embedding a password in the --out influxdb=$INFLUXDB_URL URL that test/k6/run.sh echoes to the terminal — so auth bought no confidentiality against this threat model while guaranteeing a secret in scrollback, shell history and any CI log.

Consequently INFLUXDB_USER/INFLUXDB_PASSWORD are removed from .env.example and SETUP.md — a variable nothing reads is worse than absent. Grafana's own admin credentials are untouched.

No `docker compose down -v` was needed. With auth off InfluxDB ignores the users the volume already holds, so the existing metric history survived. What was needed, and is now documented as a finding, is a deleteDatasources block: pinning a uid for a datasource whose name Grafana's sqlite volume already knows under a generated uid makes provisioning abort startup — Datasource provisioning error: data source not found, cascading through five modules to exit 1.

AC verification — by query, never by exit code

A real test/k6/run.sh SMOKE_STAGES run:

  • Zero Couldn't write stats (41 before the fix). AC-2.
  • SHOW MEASUREMENTS → 16 k6 measurements including http_req_duration and http_reqs.
  • count(value) = 221 for both, matching k6's own reported 221 requests exactly — the independent cross-check this ticket demanded instead of trusting the exit code.
  • Through Grafana's own datasource proxy at uid/InfluxDB, a percentile(value, 95) query returned a non-empty series (5 buckets, first 16.108 at 16:12:10Z) — which proves the pinned uid and the container-network URL together, not just that InfluxDB has data. AC-1.
  • 663/663 checks passed, p95 10.13 ms against the 200 ms threshold.
  • My two manual probe measurements were dropped afterwards, so the 16 are genuine k6 output.

AC-3 — the direnv reload requirement is documented in docs/performance/TRENDS.md, .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md, .env.example and SETUP.md.

AC-4 — all four disclosures retired atomically in one commit: ADR-016's Neutral consequence (rewritten to past tense, superseded by a dated amendment), the .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md blockquote, the docs/performance/TRENDS.md blockquote, and CHANGELOG.md's ### Known issues section (deleted; the entry moved to ### Fixed, and a dangling "see Known issues" cross-reference fixed). The replacement is not silence — the k6 exit-0 trap is a property of k6 and did not go away, so both rule and TRENDS blockquotes now carry a standing "verify by query, never by exit code" warning with the SHOW MEASUREMENTS command.

Gates

./mvnw clean verify cold and serial: exit 0, 1360 tests, 0 failures, coverage met (96% instruction / 88% branch). All eight prose gates ran, AdrIndexConsistencyTest included, which is what holds the amended ADR status line against docs/adr/README.md.

All five DoD gates returned VERDICT: APPROVE. Three MINOR findings were remediated in d710ed4 (a stale INFLUXDB_* instruction in SETUP.md, a misattributed ADR-043 citation in CHANGELOG.md, and a missing EOP-154 entry in ADR-016's ## Related); @security-auditor and @code-reviewer were then re-dispatched against d710ed4 and both approved again. Two reviewer claims were checked rather than accepted: a red-build report that proved to be an artefact of five agents building concurrently in one worktree, and an assertion that ADR-016 cites ADR-043 at line 255 — grep -c returns 0.

No secret value appears anywhere in the diff; the only credential-shaped lines are removals.

Deliberately deferred → EOP-161

Nothing mechanically keeps the datasource uid in step with the ten dashboard panel references, nor holds INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED at "false". Two of this story's three faults were exactly that class of unguarded cross-file mismatch, so a consistency gate is warranted — filed as EOP-161 along with pinning grafana/grafana:latest.
